articles.title: Open to investigation: On the challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Public functionaries must not use privacy to seek exemption from scrutiny

The Digital News Publishers Association’s (DNPA) challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 , and its Rules , has drawn attention to concerns that a law to safeguard informational privacy risks creating a serious chilling effect on the media. The absence of a specific exemption for journalistic activity could subject reporters investigating official misconduct or corruption to the obligations of a “data fiduciary”, requiring them to notify and seek consent from the very individuals they are investigating. Such onerous requirements could affect investigations undertaken in the public interest. The implications extend to routine newsgathering too, where personal information is integral to reporting. The omission is particularly consequential because the drafts in 2018, 2019 and 2021 carried a journalistic exemption. The Act already provides exemptions for certain forms of data processing, including for research and statistical purposes, making the denial of similar protection to journalists difficult to justify. Non-compliance can attract penalties of up to ₹250 crore, posing an existential threat to smaller and independent newsrooms. The DNPA petition also challenges Section 44(3), which amended the RTI Act, 2005, removing the earlier public-interest qualification concerning disclosure of personal information. The protection of personal information must not be absolute; an overriding public interest must remain a legitimate ground for disclosure, particularly when the information is held by public authorities. Investigations into corruption often rely on asset disclosures and tender documents containing personal data. Restricting access to these records risks reducing journalism to merely reproducing government releases.

The Supreme Court, while issuing notice on the petition, rightly emphasised the need to balance press freedom with the right to privacy. Although journalists in India enjoy no specific statutory protection for their work, freedom of the press is constitutionally protected under Article 19(1)(a). The Court has also shielded newspapers from arbitrary state restrictions. However, growing mistrust of legacy media and the rise of independent content creators have made it difficult to determine who receives such protection. The Centre has also flagged this concern. The Digital News Publishers Association’s (DNPA) challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 , and its Rules , has drawn attention to concerns that a law to safeguard informational privacy risks creating a serious chilling effect on the media. The absence of a specific exemption for journalistic activity could subject reporters investigating official misconduct or corruption to the obligations of a “data fiduciary”, requiring them to notify and seek consent from the very individuals they are investigating. articles.title: Deemed ineligible: On the Supreme Court and SIR
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court has pointed to the SIR’s flaws by design

At Wednesday’s hearing of a petition on the Delhi SIR in the Supreme Court, Justice Joymalya Bagchi asked questions that cut to the heart of the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s SIR of electoral rolls . If an existing voter was “lax, inert or did not respond” to enumeration forms, was that a ground for the ECI to “forfeit his or her right to vote forever”? The Bench headed by the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said that the ECI was in “error” to force such voters, struck off for not returning enumeration forms, to reapply on Form 6 as if they were new voters. It asked why voters who had shifted residences could not just disclose details and why deleted voters could not fill enumeration forms belatedly. This is the central design flaw of the SIR as it shifts the burden of enrolment from the state to the elector, including those who have voted before, and treats a mere change of address as ground for deletion. The share of draft deletions recorded as “shifted” or “absent” rose from 55% in Bihar to 72% in States/Union Territories in Phase 3. In Karnataka, about 84 lakh electors were deleted, marked as “shifted” or “absent” during enumeration. But only a net of 8.2 lakh, including new electors, were added during the claims phase, with the final roll being 64.5 lakh short of the projected adult population. Requiring moved voters to re-register as fresh applicants defeats the ECI’s historic mandate of widening the franchise, which was inherent in the 2002-03 intensive revision, where enumerators enrolled shifted voters at their new homes and the Chief Electoral Officer reconciled the old entries.

Justice Bagchi also mentioned that the Bihar judgment was not a “binding precedent” and that the legality of “logical discrepancy” checks, allowed only as an “interim arrangement” in West Bengal, had not been finally adjudicated. No statute or rule provides for judging a voter’s eligibility on the basis of family size or the age gap between voters and parents, which were two of the ECI’s ludicrous and algorithm-driven “logical discrepancy” checks. In West Bengal these checks resulted in massive disenfranchisement and The Hindu’s analysis found that in Delhi, Muslims were disproportionately flagged. But the Court should not merely issue managerial fixes such as extended deadlines or displaying printed lists in blocks, as it has in the past. The final SIR rolls are erroneous as deletions flowed from a flawed design rather than just lapses by the ECI. The dead and duplicate entries that the SIR identified should be removed and newly eligible electors added. Voters wrongly removed from draft rolls must be included again. The larger questions over the Commission’s SIR conduct and how its members are appointed must also be settled.

articles.title: United stand: On protests against SIR
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Protests against SIR are a recognition that it could subvert popular will

The gathering of hundreds of thousands of people at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan, organised by the Congress-led INDIA bloc parties, was a milestone in the battle for the restoration of the integrity of India’s election process. As more and more skeletons tumble out the of the closet of the Election Commission of India (ECI), its chief Gyanesh Kumar has chosen silence while the ruling BJP has rushed to shield him from criticism. The united outcry of protest by the Opposition, led by the Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi , is a strong signal of public opinion for the ruling party and India’s institutions, including the ECI, that appear complicit in a scheme that threatens the foundations of Indian democracy. What remains unexplained by the ECI and Mr. Kumar are malpractices in the Special Intensive Revision that could have the effect of subverting the popular will. Protestors on Sunday had arrived from all parts of India, and included people directly affected by the SIR across the country.

The protest reinforced Mr. Gandhi’s central role as the key challenger of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr. Gandhi, for all his faults, has been an uncompromising champion of constitutional values and pluralism in India. The BJP caricatured him, and even non-BJP voices had bought into the idea of Mr. Gandhi being a privileged dynast out of touch with the commoner. While his ancestry is a matter of fact, so is his tenacity. All Opposition parties mobilised for the protest, but the centrality of the Congress party was unmistakable. Mr. Gandhi has a special focus on subaltern classes to be included in positions of responsibility in the party. The Sunday protest was clearly the largest show of strength in recent memory. The manner in which the Congress coordinated with the wide spectrum of the Opposition, often involving rivals in States, also indicates a clear sense of purpose and pragmatism. The call for the restoration of institutional integrity is the need of the hour; but Mr. Gandhi must be careful not to misstate the nature of the crisis. In his well-reasoned call for accountability of the ECI, Mr. Gandhi ended up questioning the legitimacy of the previous election without providing any substantive basis for his allegations. He must remember that his emergence as the voice of the Opposition places on him the responsibility of being measured in his speeches and his steps.

fullParagraphs: India must respect land rights of its people while building dams

The bureaucratic impetus for the 11.2-GW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh purportedly comes from China’s aggressive development of a 60-GW mega-dam in Tibet , stoking anxieties among Indian authorities over ‘weaponised’ transboundary waters. Beijing may be able to divert flows in the Yarlung Tsangpo river, which becomes the Brahmaputra in India, to cause drought downstream or release water en masse to trigger catastrophic floods in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. New Delhi thus imagines SUMP as a strategic buffer, but in so doing faces a dilemma it should not attempt to resolve with force. Its extant top-down approach, exemplified by deploying security forces to guard survey teams and imposing the State Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act against activists, only validates fears among locals that the state will grab their land. The region also hosts sustained protests against the Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project , expanding the indictment to Arunachal Pradesh’s model of hydroelectric power development. The eastern Himalayas are among the most tectonically active and erosion-prone landscapes in the world. The mega-dam in Tibet will comprise five cascading power stations over the river’s roughly 2,000-metre fall over 50 km. Beijing has maintained the dam will not harm countries downstream but has declined to share crucial engineering details. This is why diplomacy will be an essential part of operating SUMP, in addition to Beijing’s disputed claims on Arunachal Pradesh.

The Brahmaputra basin in Assam and Bangladesh receives most of its water from monsoon rains and tributaries downstream of the Tibetan Plateau, so China cannot straightforwardly control the river’s total flow through India. Yet since Chinese interventions would have greater consequences closer to the border, SUMP will need information about both the mega-dam’s operations and downstream inflows to plan its own operations, and Beijing has declined to share the former. SUMP thus faces many uncertainties at the outset. Despite India repeatedly raising the issue with China at the highest levels, headway has been limited to Beijing agreeing to share hydrological data on humanitarian grounds during emergencies. Planners have contemplated maintaining the SUMP reservoir at 70% to accommodate unexpected surges, but the level of protection possible if China supplies no advance warning remains unclear. This uncertainty is a thorn in the side of the government’s push against more legitimate resistance by Adi community members and civil rights groups. The need for the project does not excuse the state from following all the relevant laws and protections. The state cannot protect the nation’s needs by antagonising the nation’s people.

articles.title: Maharashtra sets up drought mitigation panel, approves ₹291.91 crore relief for flood-hit farmers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The measures follow deficient rainfall in parts of Maharashtra during 2026, prompting the government to declare drought in talukas identified under the Kharif season’s Trigger-1 assessment

The Maharashtra government on Monday (November 1, 2026) announced measures to address drought and flood-related agricultural distress across the State, constituting a high-level committee headed by the Chief Minister to oversee soil and water conservation projects in drought-affected areas and approving ₹291.91 crore in financial assistance for farmers affected by heavy rainfall and flooding between June and August 2026.

Soil and Water Conservation Minister Sanjay Rathod said the committee would monitor conservation projects undertaken through non-governmental organisations, including Paani Foundation and Chandra Foundation, as part of the state’s drought mitigation efforts. The government has also decided to revive Paani Foundation’s Water Cup competition to encourage community participation in water conservation.
The measures follow deficient rainfall in parts of Maharashtra during 2026, prompting the government to declare drought in talukas identified under the Kharif season’s Trigger-1 assessment.

According to a government resolution issued on November 2, all Deputy Chief Ministers will serve as co-chairpersons of the high-level committee, which will include ministers from departments such as agriculture, water resources, rural development and employment guarantee.

A separate executive committee, chaired by the Principal Secretary of the Water Resources Department, will coordinate implementation and meet at least once a month. Progress will be monitored using geographical information systems (GIS), satellite imagery, mobile-based monitoring systems and online dashboards.

Meanwhile, Relief and Rehabilitation Minister Makarand Jadhav Patil announced that the government had sanctioned ₹262.70 crore for crop damage affecting 3,09,289 farmers across six revenue divisions, including Pune, Nagpur, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Amravati, Konkan and Nashik.

An additional ₹29.21 crore has been approved for damage to agricultural land covering 7,675.40 hectares belonging to 34,984 farmers. The assistance will cover eligible restoration work, including the removal of sand, silt and salt deposits caused by flooding.

Crop damage compensation will be transferred directly to eligible farmers’ bank accounts, while small and marginal landowners will receive assistance for damaged agricultural land up to a maximum of two hectares, in accordance with prescribed norms.
The government has also directed district collectors to ensure that banks do not divert disaster relief payments towards loan repayments or other recoveries.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu Live updates: Landfall commences over south coastal Andhra Pradesh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chennai, northern T.N. brace for heavy rain as cyclone Murasu intensifies; at least 19 domestic flights were cancelled at Vijayawada, Tirupati and Visakhapatnam airports

In an effort to provide swift assistance to citizens affected by Cyclone Murasu, the Andhra Pradesh government’s Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) has rolled out a dedicated grievance reporting mechanism through its ‘Mana Mitra’ WhatsApp Governance platform, an official release said on Monday.

Residents in cyclone-hit regions can report emergencies and civic disruptions—such as power outages, uprooted trees, collapsed walls, waterlogging, and other distress situations—by sending a message to the dedicated WhatsApp number 9552300009.

The facility is designed to establish direct communication between citizens and administration, enabling prompt on-ground intervention and effective coordination during disaster management operations.

According to officials, citizens can report cyclone-related grievances by following a simple step-by-step process: Send a “Hi” to WhatsApp number 9552300009. Select the “Services” option from the menu. Choose “Murasu Cyclone Issues”. Click on “Report Issue” and confirm. - ANI

P.L.N. Murthy, Head of the Cyclone Warning Centre, Visakhapatnam, said the cyclone is expected to make landfall between Nellore and Narsapur, south of Ongole, between 11.30 p.m. on November 2 and 4 a.m. on November 3, 2026. The wind speed during landfall is likely to be 100-110 kmph, with gusts reaching 120 kmph. A storm surge of about 1.5-2 metres above the astronomical tide is very likely to inundate low-lying areas of South Coastal Andhra Pradesh. The maximum peak surge is expected in Bapatla and parts of Krishna and Prakasam districts.
He also warned that the storm surge could inundate low-lying areas even before landfall, as it is expected to begin three to four hours ahead of the cyclone’s landfall.
Landfall due to Cyclone Murasu was accompanied by gale winds reaching speeds of up to 110 kmph and gusting up to 120 kmph.

“The landfall process commenced at 0100 hours IST on November 3. The forward sector of the wall cloud is entering the coast, while the wall cloud region is very close to the coast,” the IMD’s official press release said.
Under the influence of the cyclone, heavy rain struck several places in the southern State.

The cyclone was centred over the west-central Bay of Bengal, close to the South Andhra Pradesh coast, about 40 km southeast of Ongole, 60 km northeast of Kavali and 70 km south of Bapatla, as of 0130 hours.
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu is likely to hold a teleconference with the Collectors of all the Cyclone Murasu-impacted districts at around 3.30 A.M.
Cyclone Murasu’s path passes near Chinaganjam in Bapatla district, located between Ongole in Prakasam district and Chirala in Bapatla district.

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi acting as a ‘toolkit’ for foreign forces says Nitin Nabin
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Targeting the Congress for “trying to spread anarchy in the entire country, by targeting constitutional institutions of the country” BJP president Nitin Nabin said had the Congress fought for the issues of the people, the people would have not rejected the party

Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) president Nitin Nabin on Monday (November 2, 2026) accused Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi of leading those trying to create “anarchy” in the country and acting as a “toolkit” for foreign forces attempting to destabilise India.

A day after the Opposition INDIA bloc, led by Mr. Gandhi’s Congress party, held a gathering at Delhi’s Ramlila Grounds over allegations of ‘vote theft’ and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), Mr. Nabin held a procession in Kolkata titled ‘Save Democracy, End Anarchy’. The march which was joined by thousands of supporters was a show of strength for the saffron party.

“Rahul Gandhi is acting as a toolkit of those forces which engineered the unrest in Nepal and other neighbouring countries. If you think you will destabilise India, if you think you will work as a toolkit for those who are destabilising Europe, those who are destabilising Bangladesh or Nepal, then know that Indian democracy is very strong ,” Mr. Nabin alleged.

The march, organised under the banner ‘Save Democracy, End Anarchy’, began at College Street and proceeded towards Dharmatala in central Kolkata, with hundreds of BJP supporters including Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and State BJP president Samik Bhattacharya joining the procession.

Targeting the Congress for “trying to spread anarchy in the entire country by targeting constitutional institutions of the country” Mr. Nabin said that if the Congress had fought for the issues of the people, the people would not have rejected the party.
“They say the democracy and Constitution are under threat whenever they lose elections, but when they win elections conducted by the same Election Commission of India,” Mr. Nabin added.
He cited the victory of Congress party in Keralam Assembly elections and asked, “Had SIR been the issue, how did Congress win in Keralam?”

The BJP leader said that all the anarchy had been eradicated from West Bengal on May 4, when the BJP came to power, defeating Mamata Banerjee. Raising questions about the new bonhomie between the Congress and Mamata Banerjee, Mr. Nabin said that during the Assembly elections, Rahul Gandhi came here and spoke against corruption and misrule of the Mamata Banerjee regime and now both are sharing the stage.
Mr. Nabin said that the Congress and its allies are not interested in the welfare of 140 crore people in the county and in interested in the well-being of only three crore infiltrators.
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, who also spoke at the culmination of the rally, said that for the BJP the SIR stood for ‘Remove Infiltrators, Save India’.

“Those who have united to save themselves from corruption, imprisonment and to protect their families and bring back the politics of appeasement should remember that the Bharatiya Janata Party was elected in West Bengal in 2026 with 2.92 crore votes. For us, SIR means ‘Remove Infiltrators, Save India’. That is why they are trying to create anarchy in the state,”Mr. Adhikari said.
The first BJP Chief Minister of West Bengal warned Opposition parties that they would face a decisive political response in the forthcoming Kolkata and Howrah municipal corporation elections.

🏛️ National & Polity 📅 03 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Rahul Gandhi acting as a ‘toolkit’ for foreign forces says Nitin Nabin

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Targeting the Congress for “trying to spread anarchy in the entire country, by targeting constitutional institutions of the country” BJP president Nitin Nabin said had the Congress fought for the issues of the people, the people would have not rejected the party

Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) president Nitin Nabin on Monday (November 2, 2026) accused Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi of leading those trying to create “anarchy” in the country and acting as a “toolkit” for foreign forces attempting to destabilise India.

A day after the Opposition INDIA bloc, led by Mr. Gandhi’s Congress party, held a gathering at Delhi’s Ramlila Grounds over allegations of ‘vote theft’ and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), Mr. Nabin held a procession in Kolkata titled ‘Save Democracy, End Anarchy’. The march which was joined by thousands of supporters was a show of strength for the saffron party.

“Rahul Gandhi is acting as a toolkit of those forces which engineered the unrest in Nepal and other neighbouring countries. If you think you will destabilise India, if you think you will work as a toolkit for those who are destabilising Europe, those who are destabilising Bangladesh or Nepal, then know that Indian democracy is very strong ,” Mr. Nabin alleged.

The march, organised under the banner ‘Save Democracy, End Anarchy’, began at College Street and proceeded towards Dharmatala in central Kolkata, with hundreds of BJP supporters including Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and State BJP president Samik Bhattacharya joining the procession.

Targeting the Congress for “trying to spread anarchy in the entire country by targeting constitutional institutions of the country” Mr. Nabin said that if the Congress had fought for the issues of the people, the people would not have rejected the party.

“They say the democracy and Constitution are under threat whenever they lose elections, but when they win elections conducted by the same Election Commission of India,” Mr. Nabin added.

He cited the victory of Congress party in Keralam Assembly elections and asked, “Had SIR been the issue, how did Congress win in Keralam?”

The BJP leader said that all the anarchy had been eradicated from West Bengal on May 4, when the BJP came to power, defeating Mamata Banerjee. Raising questions about the new bonhomie between the Congress and Mamata Banerjee, Mr. Nabin said that during the Assembly elections, Rahul Gandhi came here and spoke against corruption and misrule of the Mamata Banerjee regime and now both are sharing the stage.

Mr. Nabin said that the Congress and its allies are not interested in the welfare of 140 crore people in the county and in interested in the well-being of only three crore infiltrators.

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, who also spoke at the culmination of the rally, said that for the BJP the SIR stood for ‘Remove Infiltrators, Save India’.

“Those who have united to save themselves from corruption, imprisonment and to protect their families and bring back the politics of appeasement should remember that the Bharatiya Janata Party was elected in West Bengal in 2026 with 2.92 crore votes. For us, SIR means ‘Remove Infiltrators, Save India’. That is why they are trying to create anarchy in the state,”Mr. Adhikari said.

The first BJP Chief Minister of West Bengal warned Opposition parties that they would face a decisive political response in the forthcoming Kolkata and Howrah municipal corporation elections.

articles.title: Amit Shah backs SIR, alleges 3 crore ‘illegal infiltrators’ identified in 13 crore deleted voters
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Monday alleged that the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise had identified around three crore ‘unaccounted voters’, whom he described as ‘illegal infiltrators from Bangladesh’, among the 13 crore names removed from electoral rolls. He asserted that all such infiltrators would be expelled from the country.

Addressing a public meeting at MJ Market in Hyderabad’s Old City after a ‘Save democracy-Remove anarchy’ foot march , Mr. Shah claimed that of the nearly 13 crore names deleted from voter lists during the SIR process, 4.25 crore voters were registered in two different locations, three crore were deceased, and another one crore were duplicate entries. He questioned if such names should continue to remain on the electoral rolls. “Do we need to remove infiltrators from the country’s voter lists or not?” he asked.

The Home Minister accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of defending the alleged three crore ‘unaccounted’ voters. “No matter how hard Rahul Gandhi or Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy may try, the BJP is committed to driving every infiltrator out of the country,” he said.

Mr. Shah alleged that the Congress and other Opposition parties were opposing the SIR exercise to protect ‘infiltrators from Bangladesh’, whom he described as their ‘vote bank’ and maintained that only genuine Indian citizens should be included in electoral rolls.

Ridiculing Sunday’s joint rally of Opposition parties in New Delhi, Mr. Shah described it as a ‘Save Infiltrators’ rally and urged BJP workers to counter what he termed ‘fear-mongering’ by the former on the SIR exercise through a door-to-door campaign.

The Congress was determined to halt SIR while the BJP would continue to support it, he said. Mr. Shah said the Centre was prepared to convene a special session of Parliament to discuss the issue and challenged Mr. Rahul Gandhi to participate in a debate. He said the Congress leader was not allowing Parliament to function. Taking a swipe at Mr. Gandhi, he remarked that while he might become Prime Minister in a ‘mock Parliament’, he would never attain the position in reality.

Defending the BJP’s electoral record, the Union Minister noted that Prime Minister Narendra Modi had won the 2014, 2019 and 2024 Lok Sabha elections without any SIR exercise. He also rejected allegations about Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs), asking how the Congress had won elections in Telangana, Kerala and Himachal Pradesh if the machines were flawed.

Turning his attention to Telangana, Mr. Shah alleged that the Congress government had become an ‘ATM’ for the party through the so-called ‘RR tax’. He accused the State government of failing to implement its six election guarantees and predicted that voters would reject the party in the next election.

Earlier, Mr. Shah led a foot march from the Babu Jagjivan Ram statue near Nizam College in Fateh Maidan to the meeting venue. Flanked by senior Telangana BJP leaders, including State president N. Ramchander Rao, Union Minister G. Kishan Reddy and Union Minister of State for Home Bandi Sanjay Kumar, he marched amid tight security and chants of ‘Jai Shri Ram’ and ‘Bharat Mata Ki Jai’. He had arrived by a special aircraft from Delhi and was received by the party leaders at Begumpet airport. From there he offered prayers at the Bhagyalakshmi temple at Charminar before the programme.

articles.title: Eight labourers electrocuted after machine touches power line
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Villagers said power lines were touching trees and claimed that no staff member was available at the Grid Sub-Station when they called to have the power supply disconnected

Eight labourers were electrocuted and five others injured when a road construction machine came into contact with an overhead 11 KV high-tension power line at Chhapoli village in Rajasthan’s Jhunjhunu district on Monday (November 2, 2026). The gravel mixing machine was being used to build a road with public participation.

Chhapoli village is near the Sikar-Neem Ka Thana State Highway and falls under the Udaipurwati police station area. Work on a narrow road connecting Chhapoli to Kadamkund was underway when a hydraulic jack made contact with the power line.

A massive electric current spread through the equipment instantly, striking labourers at the site. Five workers died on the spot, while three others succumbed during treatment. All the deceased were residents of Chhapoli village.

Villagers rushed to the spot and helped in the rescue efforts, as those injured were shifted to the Community Health Centre at Udaipurwati. The incident triggered anger among villagers, who staged a demonstration, alleging negligence by the administration and the power discom.
The protesters said power lines and poles were touching trees and claimed that no staff member was available at the Grid Sub-Station when they called to have the power supply disconnected.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has expressed his grief and announced ex-gratia assistance of ₹2 lakh each from the PM’s National Relief Fund to the next of kin of each deceased person. The injured will receive ₹50,000 each.

Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma has ordered a high-level inquiry into the accident and instructed officials to provide all possible relief to the affected families, besides seeking a factual report from the District Collector. Minister of State for Urban Development Jhabar Singh Kharra has been deputed to visit the accident site.
Veteran Congress leader and former CM Ashok Gehlot said a thorough investigation was essential to determine how the mishap had occurred and fix accountability for the deaths.

articles.title: M.P. Police inspector mowed down by truck carrying illicit liquor in Dewas; racket supplying liquor to Gujarat uncovered
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to police, the liquor was being smuggled from Harda district to Gujarat; truck owner arrested, driver remains at large

An inspector of Madhya Pradesh Police was on Monday mowed down in Dewas district by a truck that he had intercepted on suspicion of smuggling illegal liquor, police said on Monday. The officer has been identified as Khategaon police station in-charge Dilip Puri.
An investigation launched following the incident has uncovered an illicit trade network spanning in multiple districts of Madhya Pradesh that supplies liquor to Gujarat.

According to the police, the incident took place around 1.30 a.m. on Indore-Betul highway when Mr. Puri was leading one of the four teams formed based on intelligence inputs that large amounts of illicit liquor was being transported from Harda district’s Timarni to Gujarat.
During the checking, a parked truck was spotted near Sandalpur in Dewas district and Mr. Puri had asked the driver to step down for a search.

“The driver, however, with the intent of killing Dilip Puri, ran him over with the truck and fled the scene. Mr. Puri died during treatment. The driver also tried to run over constable Sohan Jaat, who has suffered injuries,” an official police statement said.

The driver abandoned the truck after some distance and fled the scene. Dewas Superintendent of Police Aditya Mishra said that the truck was seized and more than 1,800 litres of illicit liquor in about 200 cartons were recovered from it. A video of the truck’s inspection showed that the cartons had been kept in a hidden chamber, made by laying down an additional metal surface to project the vehicle as empty.

Special Director General (DG) of Police Upendra Jain, who has been deputed by Chief Minister Mohan Yadav to oversee the probe, told The Hindu that the driver has been identified as Gajendra Rawat alias Akku, a resident of Alirajpur district, and a search is on for him. He said that the vehicle had been provided by Kairam Singh Changod, also from Alirajpur, and the local police has taken him into custody and is being questioned.
Mr. Jain said that a case under BNS Sections 103(1), 109(1), 121(2), 3(5) and Section 34(2) Madhya Pradesh Excise Act, 1915, has been lodged.
The Special DG said that the investigation has been revealed that the illicit liquor was being taken from Harda to Gujarat.

Mr. Jain said that the police have identified several people involved in the illicit liquor network. They are Patendra Jaiswal, a resident of Badwani district who owns a government licensed liquor shop in Harda, and his business partners — Manish Jaiswal of Indore, Mohin Jaiswal who lives in Gujarat, and Rahul Jaiswal of Harda’s Timarni and his associate Vijay Rao, a resident of Indore.

The officer said that Mr. Rahul Jaiswal has been identified as a key accused, ran the network to supply illicit liquor to Gujarat. He and Mr. Rao have been taken into custody and are being questioned about their entire network.
Mr. Rahul Jaiswal has been identified as a Congress functionary, and is the party’s in-charge for the Khategaon Assembly seat.

articles.title: Netanyahu pressing Trump to attack Iran after midterms, says officials
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: A return to full-scale war with Iran could help Benjamin Netanyahu to form an emergency government after he and his far-right allies lost their parliamentary majority in last week's elections

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing for another wave of strikes on Iran after Tuesday's (November 3, 2026) midterm elections in the United States, according to two regional officials and a third person familiar with the matter.

A return to full-scale war with Iran could help Mr. Netanyahu to form an emergency government after he and his far-right allies lost their parliamentary majority in last week's elections. U.S. President Donald Trump has alternated between threatening major strikes while pushing for a deal with Iran.

The two officials said diplomatic efforts have made progress, with Qatari mediators holding two rounds of talks last week with Iranian officials. The two officials said the mediators are trying to advance a framework for Iran to cease its attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in return for the U.S. lifting its blockade on Iran's ports.

They said more talks are planned for this week. The two officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were discussing classified briefings they had received from American, and in one case Israeli, officials.

One official said Mr. Netanyahu was working with senior officials in the U.S. administration to persuade Mr. Trump to launch a quick but extensive air campaign and that the president does not appear to have made a decision.
Mr. Netanyahu pressed for strikes during a call over the weekend with Mr. Trump, who would not commit to taking military action, according to a person who was briefed on it.

Other U.S. allies in West Asia are warning against more strikes, saying it would destabilise the region and could lead Iran-allied Houthi rebels in Yemen to step up their attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping, a third regional official said. Iran-backed militias in Iraq could also get involved.
That official, and the person familiar with the Netanyahu-Trump call, were not authorised to speak publicly and spoke on condition of anonymity.

The Israeli government did not immediately comment. The White House did not directly respond to questions about Mr. Netanyahu and Mr. Trump's discussion of potential new strikes during the weekend call.

Mr. Trump told reporters on Sunday (November 1, 2026) that he and Mr. Netanyahu had a “very good” call the day before. He said they discussed Iran but gave no details. Mr. Netanyahu had pushed for renewed strikes even before the Israeli election as he sought to highlight his security credentials to a public deeply scarred by Hamas' October 7, 2023, attack.

Asked at a news conference on Saturday (October 31, 2026) about the possibility of new U.S. strikes on Iran and Iranian retaliation, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio would not say what would happen next but reiterated that the Trump administration prefers a diplomatic solution and that talks were ongoing.
“He hasn't made a decision,” Mr. Rubio said, referring to Mr. Trump.

articles.title: An anti-climactic outcome in the Knesset elections
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: While voters have reprimanded Benjamin Netanyahu for his flawed conduct, they seem to be willing to give him another chance

For the Israeli Knesset election hyped as “consequential” and a “day of reckoning for the October 7 Hamas attack”, the verdict points to new trends and the normalisation of trenchant nationalism. The inconclusive outcome risks disappointing most stakeholders. Israel, being at the epicentre of the ongoing regional tumult, needs a real-time analysis.

Israel’s total electorate is 7.3 million. Yet it has 38 officially recognised political parties vying for 120 Knesset seats, of which only 11 parties are likely to cross the 3.25% voting threshold needed to enter the legislature. The elections are on a proportional representation basis. The parties are currently arrayed in three coalitions: the ruling extreme right, the centrist bloc and the Israeli-Arab bloc which got 53, 48 and 19 seats, respectively. The last group representing a 21% minority is largely untouchable for mainstream Jewish parties. The electorate is also split along ethnic and origin-based lines into occidental, oriental and orthodox cohorts. Since the last elections in 2022, nearly half a million new voters have come of age. The voter turnout jumped by nearly a tenth to 77.7% — a sign of sharp political engagement.

Global & Diplomatic Brief: An anti-climactic outcome in the Knesset elections. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and proactive engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

Geopolitical Significance: Strengthening strategic partnerships across the Indo-Pacific, Global South, and multilateral forums such as the UN, G20, BRICS, and SCO remains central to India's foreign policy.

articles.title: Many U.K. social care migrant workers to get PR in five years under softer immigration overhaul
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Under the scheme, finalised on November 2, social care workers earning at least £25,000 per year, who arrived in the U.K. before May 2025, would be eligible for ‘indefinite leave to remain’ (ILR) after five years

Foreign social and home care workers, who arrived in the U.K. before May 2025, will be able to normally settle (become permanent residents) in five years, rather than in 15 years, as was first proposed in the British government’s ‘earned settlement’ scheme announced in November 2025.

Those earning more than £50,271 per annum, doctors, nurses and teachers will be able to settle in five years, while those earning more than £1,25,140 per annum could settle in three years, as was proposed in the November 2025 draft rules.

The news of softer final rules for care workers is likely to impact thousands of Indians who came in on the Health and Care Worker visa scheme, which began in October 2020 and ran until July 2025. The scheme is associated with reports of Indian care workers – including many from Kerala – being subject to abuse, including unpaid wages, illegal recruitment fees, threats and other forms of exploitation at the hands of employers.

Under the scheme, finalised on Monday (November 2, 2026), social care workers earning at least £25,000 per year, who arrived in the U.K. before May 2025, would be eligible for ‘indefinite leave to remain’ (ILR) after five years. Those who have fallen afoul of the initial visa conditions would be given “a second chance”, U.K. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said, with a fresh five-year qualifying period.

“The government has already stripped around 1,800 exploitative employers of their licenses,” Ms. Mahmood said on Monday (November 2, 2026), adding that the government would help workers find positions with legitimate care providers.

The softening of the conditions for residency in the final version of the earned settlement rules, announced by Ms. Mahmood, was a response to pressure from the left flank of the Labour Party and health unions, as well as a response to a public consultation on the draft policy, conducted earlier this year. The U.K. government said that over 2,02,000 responses were received, most (73%) of whom were visa holders.

The government had originally announced the draft earned settlement scheme under pressure from the parties on the right, especially Reform U.K., which, at the time, was surging in popularity. The basis of the overhaul was to increase the default qualifying period for settlement from five to ten years, with various factors either adding to or lowering the default qualifying duration of time.

The government, headed at the time by Prime Minister Keir Starmer, had argued the immigration overhaul was necessary to counter the surge in migration (sometimes called the ‘Boriswave’) in the social care and student categories that happened after Covid, during the administration of Boris Johnson, a Conservative.

Net migration hit a record of 9,44,000 in the year ending March 2023. However, following a tightening in policy started by the Rishi Sunak government and continued by Mr. Starmer’s Labour government, the net figure as of December 2025 dropped to 1,71,000.

“10 billion pounds. That is the cost of today’s U-turn,” shadow (i.e., opposition) Home Secretary Chris Philp said in the House of Commons on Monday (November 2, 2026), using Ms. Mahmood’s own cost estimate against her. He alleged that Ms. Mahmood was not in control of the government’s immigration policy and that Housing Secretary Angela Rayner, who is a prominent figure on Labour’s left, was in charge.

Other low-income workers could now obtain ILR in 10 years rather than the 15 years proposed under the draft scheme announced last year. Those with ILR have the right to live and work in the U.K. permanently and to potentially apply for benefits (public assistance).

The qualifying period for refugees and those arriving in the U.K. via illegal routes, would range from five to 30 years depending on whether they were studying, working, and how they arrived in the county.

articles.title: How AI training models could compromise privacy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Credible studies have shown that querying an AI model with ‘anonymised’ data to extract personal details that it had memorised during training can be used to identify individuals and build their profiles

The right to privacy is a constitutional right upheld by the Supreme Court in 2017. However, the legal instruments currently in place to safeguard this right seem inadequate, especially considering the technological revolution led by Artificial Intelligence (AI) around the world. While AI regulation is one of the most commonly discussed issues within governments today, the recommendations have been broad, vague and have only led to further questions. AI has immense potential to boost productivity and have positive effects on people’s lives; any indiscriminate regulatory or policy measure risks inhibiting innovation and economic growth. However, there are lower hanging fruits; specific gaps that can be filled to better safeguard people’s constitutional rights without permanently losing out in the AI race.

The Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act was passed in 2023, with the DPDP Rules being notified in November 2025. The implementation is phased with some provisions on consent and safety becoming effective only in 2027. Prior to the DPDP Act, the primary legal instrument to regulate the use and management of personal data was the Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000. Together the IT Act, 2000 and its 2011 Rules broadly regulated the export of “sensitive personal data” on the condition that the recipient ensured a level of data protection required under Indian law, and that the transfer was either necessary to perform a lawful contract or had been consented to by the data provider. An assertion and claim were sufficient to record adequacy. The criminal penalty for unauthorised disclosure was capped at three years’ imprisonment or a fine of ₹5 lakh. These penalties only applied to disclosure of sensitive personal data that were listed in the Rules such as financial data, medical or health details, sexual orientation, biometric information etc. The Rules did not apply to personal data such as names, addresses, phone numbers, caste, religion, political affiliations, browsing history, social media activity, online or offline behavioural patterns, institutional affiliations etc.

Scientific & Technical Core: Innovations led by ISRO, DRDO, CSIR, and national research institutes are advancing India's capabilities in space exploration, quantum computing, biotechnology, and clean energy.

AI has immense potential to boost productivity and have positive effects on people’s lives; any indiscriminate regulatory or policy measure risks inhibiting innovation and economic growth. However, there are lower hanging fruits; specific gaps that can be filled to better safeguard people’s constitutional rights without permanently losing out in the AI race.

• The Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act was passed in 2023, with the DPDP Rules being notified in November 2025. The implementation is phased with some provisions on consent and safety becoming effective only in 2027. Prior to the DPDP Act, the primary legal instrument to regulate the use and management of personal data was the Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000. Together the IT Act, 2000 and its 2011 Rules broadly regulated the export of “sensitive personal data” on the condition that the recipient ensured a level of data protection required under Indian law, and that the transfer was either necessary to perform a lawful contract or had been consented to by the data provider. articles.title: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary’s appeal to give up free electricity triggers row
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tejashwi Yadav has been continuously criticising the Samrat Choudhary-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government, claiming it to be “on the verge of bankruptcy”
Threats looming large over 125 units of free electricity given by Bihar government to the consumers after the appeal by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary to voluntarily give up the free benefits.
On Sunday (November 2, 2026), Mr. Choudhary appealed to the financially well-off and taxpayers in the State to give up free electricity for the development of the State.

The Chief Minister’s remarks has initiated that in days to come, the free electricity benefits may come to an end. Ahead of the assembly election in Bihar, the then Chief Minister Nitish Kumar on July 17, 2025 had announced to give 125 free units of electricity.

“In Bihar, everyone, from the rich to the poor, is being provided with 125 units of free electricity. The State government is spending between ₹8,000 and ₹10,000 per family annually in the form of an electricity subsidy, which makes ₹23,000 crore on electricity subsidy annually,” Mr. Choudhary said while addressing a two-day Pataliputra National Youth Parliament 2.0 in Patna.
He further said, “I will appeal to those who are well-off, affluent, or taxpayers to voluntarily forgo the benefit of the 125 units of free electricity and contribute to the development of Bihar.”

The Chief Minister also cited the example of Uttar Pradesh to prove his point and asserted that the population of the State is nearly double of Bihar, despite that the expenditure on electricity subsidies there is around ₹6,000 crores.

Free electricity is given under Mukhyamantri Vidhyut Upbhokta Sahayata Yojna (MVUSY). Not only this, under Mukhya Mantri Mahila Rozgar Yojana, state government has transferred ₹10,000 each to the bank accounts of 1.81 crore women till February 2026, as per data available. This scheme too was launched before the assembly elections.

Bihar CM pointed out that by giving up free electricity, the funds saved can be used to strengthen the education system in Bihar. Mr. Choudhary also reminded the people of Bihar how the government is giving other benefits to the people and spending crores.

He mentioned that on the scheme, like ‘Student Credit Card’, students pursuing higher education, including in fields like medicine and engineering are provided with financial assistance of up to ₹4 lakh making it ₹18,000 crore annually.

Leader of the Opposition (LoP) in the Bihar Legislative Assembly, Tejashwi Yadav, has been continuously criticising the Samrat Choudhary-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government, claiming it is “on the verge of bankruptcy”. The RJD leader had alleged that the state is facing extreme financial loss due to scams, corruption, revenue loss, a widening fiscal deficit and mounting debt.
Mr. Yadav earlier said the treasury lacks the funds to pay employee salaries, student scholarships, pensions, and dues to farmers.

A resident of the Boring Canal Road area in Patna, Sumitesh Kumar (42), who enjoys the benefits of free electricity, said, “Only the middle class and salaried people are paying the tax. From our taxes, the government is implementing the schemes. Why should we give up the free benefits? Instead of appealing to the common man, the CM should first ask his cabinet colleagues to give up the facilities which they get as lawmakers and Ministers. Reduce the perks and dearness allowance (DA) they get in their salaries.”

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu Live updates: Landfall to go on for next 2-3 hours over south coastal Andhra Pradesh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chennai, northern T.N. brace for heavy rain as cyclone Murasu intensifies; at least 19 domestic flights were cancelled at Vijayawada, Tirupati and Visakhapatnam airports

In an effort to provide swift assistance to citizens affected by Cyclone Murasu, the Andhra Pradesh government’s Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) has rolled out a dedicated grievance reporting mechanism through its ‘Mana Mitra’ WhatsApp Governance platform, an official release said on Monday.

Residents in cyclone-hit regions can report emergencies and civic disruptions—such as power outages, uprooted trees, collapsed walls, waterlogging, and other distress situations—by sending a message to the dedicated WhatsApp number 9552300009.

The facility is designed to establish direct communication between citizens and administration, enabling prompt on-ground intervention and effective coordination during disaster management operations.

According to officials, citizens can report cyclone-related grievances by following a simple step-by-step process: Send a “Hi” to WhatsApp number 9552300009. Select the “Services” option from the menu. Choose “Murasu Cyclone Issues”. Click on “Report Issue” and confirm. - ANI

P.L.N. Murthy, Head of the Cyclone Warning Centre, Visakhapatnam, said the cyclone is expected to make landfall between Nellore and Narsapur, south of Ongole, between 11.30 p.m. on November 2 and 4 a.m. on November 3, 2026. The wind speed during landfall is likely to be 100-110 kmph, with gusts reaching 120 kmph. A storm surge of about 1.5-2 metres above the astronomical tide is very likely to inundate low-lying areas of South Coastal Andhra Pradesh. The maximum peak surge is expected in Bapatla and parts of Krishna and Prakasam districts.
He also warned that the storm surge could inundate low-lying areas even before landfall, as it is expected to begin three to four hours ahead of the cyclone’s landfall.
B. Venkata Ramana, District Revenue Officer of Prakasam, requested that people remain at home until the Cyclone Murasu impact concludes.
He told The Hindu at the district Command Control Centre in Ongole that very heavy winds and rains are progressing in the district and will continue in the morning as well.

The landfall process of the Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ commenced at 1 a.m. on Tuesday, November 3, near Ongole, with the observed maximum sustained wind speed of 110 kmph to 120 kmph at the landfall point.

As of 3 a.m., the inner spiral band in the northern sector has touched the land and the wall cloud region is also entering the land, according to the official bulletin from the India Meteorological Department.

The landfall process may go on for three hours. The Severe Cyclonic Storm is now located at about 30 km southeast of Ongole, 50 km northeast of Kavali, 70 km south-southwest of Bapatla, 100 km northeast of Nellore and 140 km southwest of Machilipatnam, all in Andhra Pradesh. The system may continue to move north-northwestward after landfall.
Landfall due to Cyclone Murasu was accompanied by gale winds reaching speeds of up to 110 kmph and gusting up to 120 kmph.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu Live updates: Landfall continues in A.P.; CM Naidu likely to hold teleconference with District Collectors
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chennai, northern T.N. brace for heavy rain as cyclone Murasu intensifies; at least 19 domestic flights were cancelled at Vijayawada, Tirupati and Visakhapatnam airports

In an effort to provide swift assistance to citizens affected by Cyclone Murasu, the Andhra Pradesh government’s Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) has rolled out a dedicated grievance reporting mechanism through its ‘Mana Mitra’ WhatsApp Governance platform, an official release said on Monday.

Residents in cyclone-hit regions can report emergencies and civic disruptions—such as power outages, uprooted trees, collapsed walls, waterlogging, and other distress situations—by sending a message to the dedicated WhatsApp number 9552300009.

The facility is designed to establish direct communication between citizens and administration, enabling prompt on-ground intervention and effective coordination during disaster management operations.

According to officials, citizens can report cyclone-related grievances by following a simple step-by-step process: Send a “Hi” to WhatsApp number 9552300009. Select the “Services” option from the menu. Choose “Murasu Cyclone Issues”. Click on “Report Issue” and confirm. - ANI

P.L.N. Murthy, Head of the Cyclone Warning Centre, Visakhapatnam, said the cyclone is expected to make landfall between Nellore and Narsapur, south of Ongole, between 11.30 p.m. on November 2 and 4 a.m. on November 3, 2026. The wind speed during landfall is likely to be 100-110 kmph, with gusts reaching 120 kmph. A storm surge of about 1.5-2 metres above the astronomical tide is very likely to inundate low-lying areas of South Coastal Andhra Pradesh. The maximum peak surge is expected in Bapatla and parts of Krishna and Prakasam districts.
He also warned that the storm surge could inundate low-lying areas even before landfall, as it is expected to begin three to four hours ahead of the cyclone’s landfall.
Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar said a team from the State is on their way to Andhra Pradesh to support relief and restoration efforts in the cyclone-affected areas.
“Karnataka stands with the people of Andhra Pradesh, and we will extend every possible support during this difficult time,” he added.
A vehicle was stranded at Chintala village between Ongole and Kothapatnam in Prakasam district, as a tree fell due to heavy winds coupled with rain during Cyclone Murasu.
The district administration deployed a special team for their rescue and to remove the tree.
B. Venkata Ramana, District Revenue Officer of Prakasam, requested that people remain at home until the Cyclone Murasu impact concludes.
He told The Hindu at the district Command Control Centre in Ongole that very heavy winds and rains are progressing in the district and will continue in the morning as well.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh civic polls result LIVE | TDP takes early lead; HC clears Pulivendula count; rain, missing keys delay counting
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Counting of votes under way in 92 urban local bodies across Andhra Pradesh; results expected through the day

Because of Cyclone Murasu, the vote-counting process for the Ongole Municipal Corporation elections, which was scheduled to begin at 8 a.m. on Tuesday, began at noon at the RISE Engineering College centre in Ongole.

The counting was slightly delayed for the Nellore Municipal Corporation elections. Because of the cyclone, some staff faced difficulties in reaching the counting centres, leading to a delay in the counting process.

Speaking to the media, Nellore District Collector Himanshu Shukla said, “While the first round of counting took 90 minutes, we have taken measures to ensure that subsequent rounds are completed and announced within 60 minutes each.”

“We have made robust arrangements to ensure that the vote counting proceeds without any disruptions, despite the impact of the cyclone. The final results are expected by 6 pm. The results for the first round will be announced shortly,” he said.
Nellore.jpeg Nellore Collector Himanshu Shukla inspects the counting arrangements at DKW College in Nellore on Tuesday.
The TDP, the JSP and the CPI(M) have opened their accounts in the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) elections, winning one ward each as official results began coming in on Tuesday.
In Ward No. 1 in the Bheemunipatnam zone, TDP candidate Ippaka Varalakshmi defeated YSRCP candidate Tarada Srujana.
In Ward No. 75 in the West zone, JSP candidate Anga Sandhya Rani defeated YSRCP candidate G. Bhargavi. The JSP contested 32 wards in the GVMC elections as part of the NDA.
In Ward No. 105, CPI(M) candidate M. Krishnaiah defeated TDP candidate K. Vijay Kumar.
WhatsApp Image 2026-11-03 at 12.56.09 PM.jpeg Anga Sandhya Rani, the Jana Sena Party candidate who won Ward 75 in the West zone of the GVMC. Photo: File
Ashutosh Ranka, co-convener of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), posted a video on X on Tuesday alleging booth capturing and rigging in Andhra Pradesh’s urban local body elections.

In Peddapuram municipality in Kakinada district, the Jana Sena Party (JSP) has won four wards and the TDP two. The BJP, also an NDA partner, has won one. The YSRCP has won one ward. Counting for the chairperson’s post is yet to begin. Winners have been told not to hold celebration rallies in public, citing the Model Code of Conduct.

articles.title: ‘Nobody has the guts’: H.D. Kumaraswamy dares police to take action against him in sting video case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Kumaraswamy accuses Shivakumar of conspiring to distribute ‘sleaze’ videos of Prajwal Revanna; he accuses the Bengaluru Police Commissioner of acting at the behest of the Chief Minister and questions the objectivity of the probe in the sting video case

A day after the Bengaluru City Police alleged that the ‘sting’ video targeting former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah was exchanged at his residence in Delhi, Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy on Monday (November 2, 2026) dared the police to take action against him while refuting the claim.

At his press conference, turning the tables on Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, Mr. Kumaraswamy accused him of having met and conspired with the accused to distribute “sleaze” videos of former Hassan MP Prajwal Revanna .

Accusing Bengaluru Police Commissioner Seemanth Kumar Singh of acting on the instructions of the Chief Minister, he told media persons: “Many people visit my residence, and there is no restriction on visitors. I do not know whom the Police Commissioner is referring to.”

He dared the police to summon him for investigation and said that “nobody has the guts” to touch him. He also urged the Bengaluru Police to reveal the location from where they arrested a man allegedly linked to him in the sting operation.

He said there was a suspicion that the investigation was not being conducted objectively. “The woman victim had complained to the Karnataka State Commission for Protection of Child Rights. The complaint was not acted upon then. People behind the sting went to Kerala with the mala fide intention of meeting the woman for the interview,” he added.

Incidentally, Congress leader Kripa Alva was the chairperson of the commission from 2015 to 2018 during Mr. Siddaramaiah’s first tenure. Ms. Alva, who has been interrogated by the police, has been expelled from the Congress .

“There is information that the woman who had made serious accusations against the former Chief Minister has changed her statement. If this is true, why is she not being presented before the court? If she has changed her statement, she is part of the conspiracy behind the sting operation. She too should be named as an accused,” he said.

“Instead of undertaking the investigation properly, the police are satisfied with giving a clean chit to Mr. Siddaramaiah. Why are the police still investigating if the sting operation is fake? Why has the prime accused in the sting operation, Rakesh Shetty, not been arrested yet,” he asked.

Hours before Mr. Kumaraswamy’s press conference, the Central Crime Branch (CCB) of the Bengaluru Police searched the residence and office of Power TV managing director Rakesh Shetty . The searches were carried out by multiple teams of investigators after obtaining a search warrant from a court.

articles.title: Audit flags ₹3,000 monthly drinking water burden on poor families in Bengaluru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The city extracts groundwater at nearly twice the rate at which it is replenished and loses about 400 million litres of piped water every day, according to Syed Ahmed Hussain, convenor of the Water Satyagraha campaign

With a drinking water crisis looming over Bengaluru in the coming summer months following a 43% deficit in the south-west monsoon, the Water Satyagraha campaign has flagged the mounting financial burden on economically weaker families, who increasingly depend on private water tankers to meet their daily needs.

The preliminary water audit findings of the household survey conducted by the campaign revealed that economically weaker sections, particularly residents of slums, were spending a disproportionately large share of their income on drinking water purchased from private tankers.
The campaign, whose volunteers have been conducting household surveys across different localities, has predicted a shortfall of more than 600 million litres a day (MLD) in the city’s water supply.

“Poor families spend around ₹3,000 a month on drinking water, which is higher than the ₹2,000 monthly assistance provided to women under the Gruha Lakshmi scheme of the government of Karnataka,” said Syed Ahmed Hussain, convenor of the campaign and KPCC vice-president.
Mr. Hussain pointed out that the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB) had no power to regulate the prices charged by private water tanker operators.

Bengaluru currently receives around 1,470 MLD of Cauvery water against an estimated daily demand of more than 2,100 MLD, according to the findings. The city generates around 2,120 MLD of sewage daily, of which 1,348 MLD is treated, leaving 772 MLD untreated, Mr. Hussain said.
The household survey also found that some middle-class families were spending as much as ₹54,000 annually on drinking water alone.

Sharing the preliminary findings with journalists, Mr. Hussain, who hails from Kanakapura, said, "Bengaluru contributes about 40% to Karnataka’s economy, yet many of its families have to wait for days for water to flow from their taps. The city extracts groundwater at nearly twice the rate at which it is replenished, loses about 400 million litres of piped water every day, and leaves residents of its peripheral areas dependent on private tankers that they can barely afford.”
Across Karnataka, 226 of the State’s 240 taluks have been declared drought-hit this year, while contaminated drinking water has claimed lives in Raichur, Chitradurga, and Mysuru districts, he said.

Pointing to the 772 MLD of untreated sewage generated daily, Mr. Hussain said every taluk in Bengaluru Urban district had been categorised as over-exploited in terms of groundwater extraction. Nearly 27% of the city’s piped water was lost through leakage, theft and unbilled consumption, he added.
BWSSB chairperson directs officials to prepare for possible water scarcity in Bengaluru
With 2027 in mind, BWSSB tells citizens to install aerators, use drinking water judiciously

articles.title: Initiative to strengthen perinatal mental healthcare to be piloted in T.N.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: As a part of the initiative, Village Health Nurses and medical officers are being trained to screen pregnant women for mental health problems, particularly depression, during the antenatal and postnatal periods and facilitate timely and appropriate care

Tamil Nadu is preparing to pilot an initiative to strengthen perinatal mental healthcare by making screening available at the primary healthcare level. As a part of the initiative, Village Health Nurses (VHNs) and medical officers are being trained to screen pregnant women for mental health problems, particularly depression, during the antenatal and postnatal periods and facilitate timely and appropriate care.

The ‘Thai Manam’ project is set to be piloted, with VHNs and medical officers in four blocks of Villupuram district — Kanai, Koliyanur, Vallam, and Mugaiyur — who are undergoing training as part of a collaborative initiative involving the Institute of Mental Health (IMH), Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Epidemiology, and the Directorate of Public Health (DPH) and Preventive Medicine.

articles.title: Maharashtra FDA confiscates Patanjali stock, suspends licences
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The FDA seized 2,279.7 litres of ghee worth ₹20.20 lakh from Divya Mahavitarak, a Patanjali distributor, in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. Officials suspect the stock may have been misbranded or adulterated

The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) of Maharashtra carried out inspections across the State between October 28 and 31. The department took away 19 licences. It confiscated items weighing 3,53,000 kg. The items held a value of ₹9.01 crore. The drive resulted in 13 FIRs and 16 arrests. FDA Commissioner Tukaram Munde headed the department during this period.

The FDA seized 2,279.7 litres of ghee worth ₹20.20 lakh from Divya Mahavitarak, a Patanjali distributor, in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. Officials suspect the stock may have been misbranded or adulterated.
The department took 1,44,218kg of oil from Avenue Supermarts in Bhiwandi. It also took 20,560kg of items from Amin Traders in Satara.

The department closed 7 establishments and took 6 vehicles. The actions occurred due to a lack of hygiene and violations of rules regarding safety. These establishments include units that make namkeen, sweets, and spices. These units operate in Mumbai, Amravati, and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu LIVE updates: Eye of cyclone crosses Andhra Pradesh coast
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Cyclone is expected to subside into a deep depression by Tuesday (November 3, 2026) midnight with wind speeds reaching up to 75 kmph

In an effort to provide swift assistance to citizens affected by Cyclone Murasu, the Andhra Pradesh government’s Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) has rolled out a dedicated grievance reporting mechanism through its ‘Mana Mitra’ WhatsApp Governance platform, an official release said on Monday.

Residents in cyclone-hit regions can report emergencies and civic disruptions—such as power outages, uprooted trees, collapsed walls, waterlogging, and other distress situations—by sending a message to the dedicated WhatsApp number 9552300009.

The facility is designed to establish direct communication between citizens and administration, enabling prompt on-ground intervention and effective coordination during disaster management operations.

According to officials, citizens can report cyclone-related grievances by following a simple step-by-step process: Send a “Hi” to WhatsApp number 9552300009. Select the “Services” option from the menu. Choose “Murasu Cyclone Issues”. Click on “Report Issue” and confirm. - ANI

Three districts in Telangana were placed under red alert — indicating possibility of extremely heavy rain — on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), under the impact of the severe cyclonic storm Murasu (war drum). The eye of the storm crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast at 5.30 a.m.

While Nalgonda and Nagakurnool were earlier placed under the weather alert, India Meteorological Department-Hyderabad Centre on Tuesday has forecast extremely heavy rain in Suryapet, Khammam and Bhadradri Kothagudem districts. -- The Hindu Bureau

Naguluppalapadu mandal in Prakasam district recorded the highest rainfall of 198 mm in the 24 hours ending at 8.30 a.m. on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), as Cyclone Murasu brought heavy to very heavy rainfall across several parts of the district. Kothapatnam mandal followed with 182.3 mm, while Ongole Urban recorded 174.7 mm during the same period. The cyclone hit near Kothapatnam beach on the shore of Bay of Bengal.

According to the Automatic Weather Station (AWS) rainfall data, provided by the Prakasam district Command Control Centre, five mandals received more than 100 mm of rainfall, indicating the intensity of the downpour in several parts of the district. Santhanuthalapadu recorded 110.5 mm, while J. Panguluru received 108 mm.

Chimakurthy and Ongole Rural also experienced substantial rainfall, recording 95.3 mm and 93.3 mm respectively. Addanki received 86.9 mm, followed by Singarayakonda with 85.6 mm and Maddipadu with 81.1 mm. -- The Hindu Bureau
The landfall process of severe cyclonic storm Murasu is currently underway, according to the CMO.

It is said heavy to very heavy rainfall, with extremely heavy rainfall in isolated places, is expected in Bapatla, Guntur, Krishna, Palnadu, NTR, Eluru, and West Godavari districts today (November 3, 2026).
Moderate to isolated heavy rainfall has been forecast on November 4, 2026

articles.title: After 22 years, RBI reopens UCB licensing: can new audit rules ensure a safer banking sector? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: MSC​​ARO and ICAI build guardrails for multi-state cooperatives aspiring to become banks

Once bitten, twice shy. India’s urban cooperative banks (UCBs) have had their share of troubled episodes, regulatory lapses and governance failures, which neither the Government nor the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) afford to overlook.

After keeping UCB licensing on hold for 22 years, the RBI’s decision to revive the process marks a significant shift. But this time, the Government seems determined to put the guardrails in place before allowing the sector to gather momentum.

articles.title: Child dies of measles in New York's first such death in 30 years
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The U.S. stopped the domestic spread of measles in 2000 by maintaining high vaccination rates, but they have fallen in recent years to below the 95% coverage needed to prevent outbreaks of the viral disease
A child in rural northern New York has died after contracting measles, marking the State's first death from the disease in 30 years, state officials announced on Monday (November 2, 2026).
The child died in Lewis County, about 93 miles (150 kilometres) north of Syracuse, Governor Kathy Hochul said.

The U.S. stopped the domestic spread of measles in 2000 by maintaining high vaccination rates, but they have fallen in recent years to below the 95% coverage needed to prevent outbreaks of the viral disease.

Ms. Hochul, a Democrat, said the child's death is “a devastating reminder of what's at stake when Washington deliberately erodes decades of progress in protecting Americans from preventable illnesses.”

The Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has confirmed three measles-associated deaths in the U.S. this year, but State health departments have reported higher numbers. Pennsylvania health officials have reported five deaths this year and are investigating a possible sixth.

Ms. Hochul declared a disaster emergency in early October because of measles cases in neighbouring States and in rural areas of New York. The executive order extended the pool of people who can administer measles vaccines to include paramedics, midwives and others, and it allowed nurses to join doctors in ordering testing.

articles.title: Binance’s recovery from the biggest crypto hack in history | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The largest cryptocurrency exchange in the world was hit by an approximately $6.3 billion hack, the biggest in history, yet, customers got their crypto back in about 3-4 days

The story so far: Early morning on October 29, many customers at Binance, the largest cryptocurrency exchange in the world, began receiving messages that their accounts were being unexpectedly emptied. What followed, over the course of just about 20 minutes, was the biggest crypto hack in history, with more than $6 billion worth being stolen. By November 2, Binance had replaced 100% of the stolen amount to customers. The search for the culprit and recovery process still continues, but the customer impact has been mitigated in a remarkably short time.

Cryptocurrency transactions involve a multi-rung authentication involving public keys as well as private keys that are held by each user. According to Binance, a preliminary investigation points to a “compromised” laptop belonging to one of its engineers that could have allowed the hacker to submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions.
