articles.title: California could become the first State to tax billionaires' wealth
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Proposition 40 would impose a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of Californians whose net worth exceeds $1 billion, with most of the revenue dedicated to replacing federal funding cuts to healthcare

California could become the first State in the nation to tax the net worth of billionaires , it was proposed on Tuesday (November 3. 2026) under a ballot measure that has divided liberal leaders nationally and triggered one of the most expensive ballot fights in the State’s history as the ultra-rich scramble to figure out whether they would pay the tax or flee.
Proposition 40 would impose a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of Californians whose net worth exceeds $1 billion, with most of the revenue dedicated to replacing federal funding cuts to healthcare.

Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders has framed the proposal as a monumental step toward reining in deep wealth inequality by ensuring the ultra-rich pay their fair share. But Democratic Governor Gavin Newsom warns it would prompt the State's wealthiest to move out of California and take their tax money with them.

The “no” side has raised roughly 10 times as much as the “yes” side, thanks in large part to tech moguls and venture capitalists, who have poured millions into a political action committee fighting the measure. Billionaires are already bracing for its approval. Some of them, including Google co-founders Sergey Brin and Larry Page, started cutting ties with the State after the measure was unveiled. Mark Zuckerberg said he would stay in California for eight years and made a deal with Meta that would help him pay the tax without losing his ownership stake in the company.

Backers of the proposed tax, led by the powerful labor union SEIU United Healthcare Workers West, say it's needed to help the State backfill the federal funding cuts. The union estimates the state will lose $100 billion in federal healthcare funding over five years.
“It's time to collect those taxes so we can ensure that our healthcare system is still safe,” said Lorena Gonzalez, president of the California Federation of Labor Unions.

But some traditional Democratic allies, including Planned Parenthood and the California Teachers Association, are part of a coalition opposing it. They're concerned about how the tax revenue would be divvied up and about the potential impact on the State's budget if there's a mass exodus of wealthy taxpayers. California's budget relies heavily on the income tax of the State's richest residents.

Likely voters were slightly more likely to oppose the measure than support it in a poll conducted in mid-October by the Public Policy Institute of California, with 52% saying they would vote “no” and 46% saying they would vote “yes.” That's an apparent shift from a PPIC survey conducted in early September, when 52% of likely voters said they'd vote for the tax and 46% said they'd vote against it.
Robert Swonger, an auto glass technician living near Sacramento who's politically independent, said he planned to vote against it.
“Obviously, I would like billionaires not to have as much money as they do,” he said. “But I don't believe taxing them out of existence is going to work.”

Anthony Serrano, a Democrat living in Folsom who works for Kaiser Permanente, one of the nation's largest not-for-profit healthcare plans, said he was leaning toward voting for the tax because he tends to support “anything that is a positive for healthcare.”

Even if the measure wins approval from a majority of voters, it would be blocked from taking effect if at least one of two measures designed to nullify it, which are also on this year's ballot, passes and receives more “yes” votes. The proposals, which are backed by the political action committee Building a Better California, include a ban on new taxes on financial assets and other personal property, a category that excludes real estate. The committee has raised more than $333 million, about 30% of it from Brin.

California could become the first State in the nation to tax the net worth of billionaires , it was proposed on Tuesday (November 3. 2026) under a ballot measure that has divided liberal leaders nationally and triggered one of the most expensive ballot fights in the State’s history as the ultra-rich scramble to figure out whether they would pay the tax or flee.

Proposition 40 would impose a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of Californians whose net worth exceeds $1 billion, with most of the revenue dedicated to replacing federal funding cuts to healthcare.

Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders has framed the proposal as a monumental step toward reining in deep wealth inequality by ensuring the ultra-rich pay their fair share. But Democratic Governor Gavin Newsom warns it would prompt the State's wealthiest to move out of California and take their tax money with them.

The “no” side has raised roughly 10 times as much as the “yes” side, thanks in large part to tech moguls and venture capitalists, who have poured millions into a political action committee fighting the measure. Billionaires are already bracing for its approval. Some of them, including Google co-founders Sergey Brin and Larry Page, started cutting ties with the State after the measure was unveiled. Mark Zuckerberg said he would stay in California for eight years and made a deal with Meta that would help him pay the tax without losing his ownership stake in the company.

Backers of the proposed tax, led by the powerful labor union SEIU United Healthcare Workers West, say it's needed to help the State backfill the federal funding cuts. The union estimates the state will lose $100 billion in federal healthcare funding over five years.

“It's time to collect those taxes so we can ensure that our healthcare system is still safe,” said Lorena Gonzalez, president of the California Federation of Labor Unions.

But some traditional Democratic allies, including Planned Parenthood and the California Teachers Association, are part of a coalition opposing it. They're concerned about how the tax revenue would be divvied up and about the potential impact on the State's budget if there's a mass exodus of wealthy taxpayers. California's budget relies heavily on the income tax of the State's richest residents.

Likely voters were slightly more likely to oppose the measure than support it in a poll conducted in mid-October by the Public Policy Institute of California, with 52% saying they would vote “no” and 46% saying they would vote “yes.” That's an apparent shift from a PPIC survey conducted in early September, when 52% of likely voters said they'd vote for the tax and 46% said they'd vote against it.

Robert Swonger, an auto glass technician living near Sacramento who's politically independent, said he planned to vote against it.

“Obviously, I would like billionaires not to have as much money as they do,” he said. “But I don't believe taxing them out of existence is going to work.”

Anthony Serrano, a Democrat living in Folsom who works for Kaiser Permanente, one of the nation's largest not-for-profit healthcare plans, said he was leaning toward voting for the tax because he tends to support “anything that is a positive for healthcare.”

Even if the measure wins approval from a majority of voters, it would be blocked from taking effect if at least one of two measures designed to nullify it, which are also on this year's ballot, passes and receives more “yes” votes. The proposals, which are backed by the political action committee Building a Better California, include a ban on new taxes on financial assets and other personal property, a category that excludes real estate. articles.title: India, Israel vote against UNGA draft on regional conventional arms control
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: India and Israel were the only countries to vote against the resolution in the 193-member UN body

India and Israel have voted against a draft resolution in the United Nations by Pakistan and Belarus on conventional arms control at regional and subregional levels, with New Delhi saying countries' security concerns are not confined within regional boundaries.

The draft resolution, titled ‘General and complete disarmament: Conventional arms control at the regional and subregional levels’, was approved by the UN General Assembly’s First Committee on Monday (November 2, 2026) with 180 votes in favour, two against and no abstentions.
India and Israel were the only countries to vote against the resolution in the 193-member UN body.
Explaining India's vote, First Secretary at India’s Permanent Mission to the UN, Anmol Sher Bedi said conventional arms control was a global issue.
“We are not fully convinced that it should be pursued primarily in regional and sub-regional contexts,” Bedi said while delivering India’s Explanation of Vote in the UNGA First Committee.
He said New Delhi voted against the resolution consistent with its past position.

India also questioned the resolution's request to the UN Disarmament Commission to consider formulating principles that could serve as a framework for regional agreements on conventional arms control.
“We read this request with a certain degree of curiosity,” Bedi said.

He pointed out that the Commission had already adopted by consensus guidelines and recommendations on regional disarmament in 1993, guidelines on conventional arms control and disarmament in 1999, and recommendations on practical confidence-building measures in the field of conventional weapons in 2017.
“That makes three consensus outcomes on this very subject in the very body now being asked to start from scratch,” he said.
“We fail to understand why a subject already deliberated at length needs another round of deliberation unless the aim is to keep the UN disarmament machinery busy,” Bedi added.
Bedi also objected to the resolution's approach towards maintaining a balance in defence capabilities within a region or subregion.

articles.title: Who are the Indian-origin candidates in U.S. midterm elections?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Democratic lawmakers Ro Khanna, Pramila Jayapal, Ami Bera and Suhas Subramanyam are seeking re-election to the U.S. Congress
Indian-origin candidates are seeking office across the United States in the November 3, 2026, midterm elections, the polls are so called because they fall midway through a President’s four-year term

All 435 seats in the House of Representatives are due for election, since members serve two-year terms. In the Senate, where members serve six years, 35 of the 100 seats are up for election, including special elections in Ohio and Florida.

The Indian-origin candidates are contesting from States including California, Washington, Virginia, Arizona, Florida, Texas, Ohio, New York and Maryland. Their races span different levels of government, from the U.S. Congress and State executive offices to city leadership positions.

Several Indian-Americans are in the fray across Texas, Florida, Arizona, Ohio, New York and Los Angeles. Democratic lawmakers Ro Khanna, Pramila Jayapal, Ami Bera and Suhas Subramanyam are seeking re-election to the U.S. Congress.
Here are some of the prominent Indian-origin candidates contesting the midterm elections

Congressman Khanna is a member of the progressive wing of the Democratic Party. His grandfather, Amarnath Vidyalankar, was a freedom fighter who was imprisoned alongside Mahatma Gandhi and later served as a Congress Member of Parliament.

Mr. Khanna is a second-generation immigrant. His father, a chemical engineer from the Indian Institute of Technology, and his mother, a school teacher, migrated to the United States from Punjab. Born in Philadelphia, Mr. Khanna studied economics at the University of Chicago before earning a law degree from Yale Law School. He later worked as an intellectual property lawyer with clients from the technology sector.

A Democrat from California, Mr. Khanna is seeking re-election from California’s 17th Congressional District, which includes parts of Silicon Valley. He has criticised President Donald Trump’s policies as “utterly destructive”, described him as a “lame duck”, and said Democrats would prevail in the 2026 midterm elections and the 2028 presidential election.

Congresswoman Jayapal, who was born in Chennai, is seeking another term from Washington’s 7th Congressional District. In 2020, she became the second Indian-American woman elected to the U.S. House of Representatives.
Ms. Jayapal traces her roots to Kerala. Her mother, Maya Jayapal, is a writer and counsellor and the author of Bangalore: Roots and Beyond .
Ms. Jayapal was the first Indian-American woman elected to the U.S. House of Representatives and has represented Washington’s 7th Congressional District since 2017.

On October 14, 2026, Ms. Jayapal voiced concern over reports about the removal of 13 crore names from draft electoral rolls in India. The Democratic lawmaker said she supported non-violent protests against what she described as anti-democratic efforts.

articles.title: The cow, the flea and the genome: One Health and the statecraft of prevention
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A cattle virus at home and a plague scare abroad make the same argument this World One Health Day: life is epidemiologically indivisible, and the institutions that govern and study it must learn to be so too

In the second of his Major Rock Edicts, cut into stone in the third century BCE, Ashoka records that he has provided medical care of two kinds, for people and for animals, and has had healing herbs planted wherever they were lacking. Twenty-three centuries before the phrase existed, an Indian State treated the health of humans, animals and the land as a single charge of government. Rudolf Virchow, who introduced the word ‘zoonosis’, restated the idea for the age of the microscope: between animal and human medicine there is no dividing line, nor should there be.

articles.title: Apple posts stronger-than-expected Q4 revenue in first earnings report for new CEO John Ternus
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Apple Inc. has posted stronger-than-expected revenue in the fiscal fourth quarter, giving new CEO John Ternus a positive start to his tenure that began in September

Apple Inc. posted stronger-than-expected revenue in the fiscal fourth quarter, giving new CEO John Ternus an upbeat start to his tenure, which began in September. The solid results bucked a downward trend for tech giants this quarter, as companies including Alphabet, Amazon and Intel had disappointing quarterly results.

The Cupertino, California-based company earned $30.71 billion, or $2.10 per share, in the July-September period. That's up 12% from $27.47 billion, or $1.85 per share, in the same period a year earlier. Apple said its earnings included 5 cents per share from tariff refunds.
Revenue rose 12% to $114.5 billion from $102.5 billion.
Analysts, on average, were expecting earnings of $1.99 per share on revenue of $113.4 billion, according to a poll by FactSet.

“Apple’s strong earnings come in the wake of a recent tech sell-off, as investors question the enormous cost and uncertain returns of the AI boom driven by Apple’s Big Tech counterparts," said Emarketer analyst Jacob Bourne, adding that record iPhone revenue and strong growth in China demonstrate the resilience of Apple's business.

While its rivals are facing investor uncertainty over massive investments in artificial intelligence, Bourne said Apple's “tepid approach" to AI infrastructure spending helps preserve its cash flow — while partnerships with companies like Alphabet could help Apple to strengthen its AI capabilities without taking on the same financial risks as its peers.

Despite the solid quarterly numbers, Apple said its closely watched gross margin, which was 47.9% during the fourth quarter, will be lower in the December quarter — between 45% and 46% — primarily due to higher memory costs and expenses related to its release of Siri AI.
While Apple's stock was flat after the earnings numbers came out, it declined 2.6% to $329.60 during the earnings call. The stock had closed down 1.8% at $338.32 in regular trading.

articles.title: Anthropic says revenue surged 1100% ahead of IPO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The filing also showed Anthropic has committed to spend about $895 billion, mostly on computing power, much of it over the next five years

Anthropic, one of the world's leading artificial intelligence companies, on Monday reported a more than 1,100 percent surge in quarterly revenue as it counts down to going public on Wall Street later this month.
Anthropic's listing, expected as early as next week, comes amid growing nervousness among investors about the huge sums being poured into AI.
Revenue reached $17 billion in the third quarter, up from $1.4 billion a year earlier.

The company, whose stock market debut will help determine how long the AI spending boom lifting the US economy can last, said in an amended filing that its net loss reached $23.3 billion in the July-September period.
The loss stemmed mostly from non-cash accounting charges linked to the company's rising valuation, the filing showed.
The filing also showed Anthropic has committed to spend about $895 billion, mostly on computing power, much of it over the next five years.
It slipped back to an operating loss of $567 million in the third quarter as it paid more for short-term computing capacity.

The IPO will be a major test of the market's faith in the AI boom, with the pool of potential investors set to widen as retail traders get their first chance to buy shares directly in a standalone AI giant.
Last week, skittishness about AI spending triggered a sharp sell-off in big tech stocks after the latest earnings showed massive investment without clear enough signs of a return.

Anthropic's roughly 400-page filing devotes more than 90 pages to risks, including those facing an industry that has seen a string of reports in recent months of AI systems behaving in unexpected and harmful ways.

articles.title: Google rolls out personal intelligence with experimental AI app Dreambeans in India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The application, which was built by Google Labs, creates a personalised daily collection of stories
Alphabet-owned Google has launched its experimental personal intelligence app Dreambeans in India. The application, which was built by Google Labs, creates a personalised daily collection of stories.
The app creates water-colour style imageries every day by connecting different Google applications like Photos, Email, Calendar and others that are linked to the user.

The company has said that the app processes data from Google apps that the user has opted into. If an app is not linked to Dreambeans, then information from that application is not included in the content created in the experimental AI app.
ALSO WATCH Google’s parent company Alphabet’s shares plunge 12.6%, loses almost $500 billion in market value

This standalone app was first rolled out to both Android and iOS users in the US in September. In India, Dreambeans is available on Android and iOS across 14 languages, including Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam and Hindi.
In terms of privacy, Google says that users can change apps that are connected to Dreambeans, and that they can also delete their data by clicking the profile icon in the AI app.
The company has also said that the opt-ins made in Dreambeans do not affect choices made in Gemini or AI Mode.

The search giant has also said that the app can hallucinate, and, at certain times, create stories that are incorrect. In such scenarios, the company recommends users to tap a “thumbs down” to fine-tune the app.
Dreambeans, at this point, is unlike a social media application where users can connect with others. The application’s interface looks more like a visual journal that is private to the user.
Google has not confirmed whether it plans to create a system where one user’s content is shown to others, similar to how Instagram or Facebook works.
But Google has been attempting to push its AI services, like Gemini and AI Mode, through the personal intelligence route.

With the help of apps like Dreambeans, the company is in a strong position to serve search requests in a more contextual way, as an unsuspecting user might give the application access to their apps that are linked to a particular Google account.

articles.title: As Binance reopens withdrawals, North Korea denies hacking exchange
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The FBI said at the weekend that North Korea was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion in virtual assets from Binance

North Korea on Tuesday dismissed as “absurd rhetoric” US allegations that it was behind a $6 ​billion cryptocurrency heist on the Binance platform , saying they proved Washington remained hostile towards it, state news ⁠agency KCNA said.

The denial by Kim Yo Jong, the influential sister of leader Kim Jong Un, comes as Pyongyang has stayed silent on US President Donald Trump’s overtures to resume summit diplomacy. In the wake of the US allegations, she said North Korea had “issues ‌to reconsider” over what she called US hostility.

The FBI said at the weekend that North Korea was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion in virtual assets from Binance, the world’s biggest ‌cryptocurrency exchange, in what could be the largest-ever financial heist.

“The FBI is trying to brand the DPRK ‌as ⁠a ‘cyber criminal state,’ claiming that it obtained information that a hacking organization ‘supported’ by the DPRK was involved in ⁠the incident,” KCNA quoted Kim Yo Jong, a ruling party official, as saying. DPRK is short for the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea.
“But the US assertion is absurd rhetoric and nothing new,” Kim said.
“It is a grave political provocation against the DPRK that the US misleads international public opinion ​as if all the cyber crimes in different parts ‌of the world are our deeds.”

Cybersecurity experts say North Korean hackers are among the world’s most prolific crypto thieves and the proceeds help fund the country’s weapons programmes. North Korea denies allegations linking it to cryptocurrency theft and other cybercrimes.

Analysts in Seoul said Pyongyang’s unusually swift response likely reflected concern that the allegation could lead ‌to tighter efforts to disrupt revenue streams that North Korea is accused of using to finance its weapons.

“With ​sanctions already in place, cryptocurrency theft has become one of North Korea’s key channels for securing funds for regime maintenance and weapons development,” said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University’s Institute ⁠for Far Eastern Studies.
Additional US measures targeting crypto wallets, laundering networks and cryptocurrency exchanges could choke off an important source of revenue, Lim said.

South Korea’s central bank estimated North Korea’s gross domestic product at 47.18 trillion won ($35.09 billion) in 2025, meaning the Binance ‌theft could be equivalent to about a sixth of its economic output.

Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis estimated 89% of crypto hack losses in 2026 were linked to North Korea, up from 15% in 2021. It said the average reported loss per hack rose from $50.65 million in 2021 to $185.65 million in 2026.

articles.title: Indonesia’s wildfires scorch 1.9 million hectares
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: El Niño has intensified Indonesia’s dry conditions, worsening fires and toxic haze that fuel public anger. CREA estimates 5,310 pollution-related deaths in September, with 58 million exposed to unhealthy air

Wildfires scorching Indonesia’s forests and peatlands have sent thick, toxic haze across parts of Southeast Asia, fuelling public anger over the government’s response. On October 28, thousands of Indonesians took to the streets, with protesters linking the worsening fire crisis to broader grievances over President Prabowo Subianto’s policies and handling of the country’s problems. “No Clean Air Under Dirty Government,” read one placard, while another warned: “If we burn, you burn with us.”

More than 1.9 million hectares burned across Indonesia between January and September 2026, according to Nusantara Atlas FireWatch data. The annual hotspot count in 2026 has already surpassed the yearly totals recorded every year from 2019 to 2025, with two months of the year still remaining.

The fires reflect a combination of land-clearing practices and unusually dry weather. Land is often deliberately burned to clear space for agriculture and plantations. The risks are particularly acute in peatlands, wetlands rich in partially decomposed organic matter that store large amounts of carbon. When peatlands are drained for plantations or other development, the peat dries out and becomes highly flammable. Once ignited, peat fires can smoulder underground for weeks, making them difficult to detect and extinguish while releasing large amounts of smoke.

El Niño has compounded these risks this year. Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysical Agency (BMKG) of Indonesia, in a release in September, said “the phenomenon of El Niño with very strong intensity and Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) in the ocean around Indonesia has an impact on reducing rainfall.” It said that 61.91% of the area of the Indonesian mainland is currently experiencing a dry season.

The scale of the fires is also striking when compared with previous El Niño years. By September 2026, the cumulative burned area had reached 38% higher than the 1.39 million hectares recorded by the same point in 2019 and more than double the 886,172 hectares recorded in 2023.

The fires are spread across Indonesia’s vast archipelago, extending beyond traditional hotspots in Sumatra and Kalimantan. Papua Selatan recorded the highest number of hotspots in the October 28-29 period, which coincided with nationwide protests.
Burned-area figures also show a sharp escalation between July and September in several provinces, with Papua Selatan, Kalimantan Barat and Nusa Tenggara Timur among the worst affected by September.

The Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), an independent research organisation that studies air pollution and its health impacts, estimated that air pollution-related deaths rose 42%, from 3,740 in August to 5,310 in September in Indonesia.
Of the September deaths, an estimated 3,560 were linked to smoke from forest and land fires, while 1,750 were attributed to non-fire sources, including urban and industrial pollution.

The number of people exposed to unhealthy or hazardous air reached a monthly record of 58 million, up 40% from August. CREA also estimated that high PM2.5 exposure triggered 333,470 acute respiratory infection cases across seven fire-affected provinces, with children under five accounting for nearly a quarter.

The effects of the fires extend beyond areas directly affected by the flames, worsening respiratory illnesses and air pollution in neighbouring Malaysia and Singapore. With private firms in Indonesia coming under heavy criticism for contributing to the fires with their ‘slash and burn’ activities to clear vast tracts of life, Singapore has initiated action under its Transboundary Haze Pollution Act. The foreign ministers of Indonesia and Singapore, after their meeting on October 27, said that the two countries will explore setting up a joint task force to deal with haze from Indonesia’s forest fires.

Source: Nusantara Atlas FireWatch data and Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), an independent research organisation that produces data and analysis on air pollution and its health impacts

articles.title: Cyber police book 18 for allegedly revealing identity of minor accused in Cheranalloor car crash case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kochi City Cyber police have registered a case against 18 social media handles for allegedly revealing the identity of a 17-year-old accused in the Cheranalloor luxury car crash case

The Kochi City Cyber police have registered a case against 18 social media handles for allegedly revealing the identity of a 17-year-old accused in the Cheranalloor luxury car crash case. articles.title: Ajit Doval meets Vietnam President To Lam, briefs him on visit outcomes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ajit Doval, who visited Vietnam on November 1-2, called on To Lam and conveyed the greetings of Prime Minister Narendra Modi

National Security Adviser (NSA) Ajit Doval has met Vietnam's President To Lam during his visit to Hanoi and briefed him on the outcomes of his discussions with the Southeast Asian country's senior leaders.
Mr. Doval, who visited Vietnam on November 1-2, called on Mr. Lam, who is also the General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam, and conveyed the greetings of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Mr. Doval thanked Mr. Lam "for his steadfast support in strengthening the India-Vietnam Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership," the Indian Embassy in Hanoi said in a post on X on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

During the meeting, Mr. Doval briefed the President on the outcomes of his discussions with Vietnamese leaders and recalled the Vietnamese President's State visit to India in May, according to the embassy.

The National Security Advisor also met Vietnam's Minister of Public Security General Luong Tam Quang, and the two sides discussed cooperation in law enforcement, cyber, maritime and economic security, the embassy said.
They agreed to strengthen capacity building in these areas, it said.
The embassy said the discussions reflected the "deep and mutually trusted civilisational partnership between India and Vietnam".
India, Vietnam deepen defence cooperation with focus on maritime security
The two sides also exchanged views on regional and global developments.

Mr. Doval also met Vietnam's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defence, General Phan Van Giang, to review ongoing bilateral defence cooperation and agree to strengthen engagement in the sector further.

He also met Foreign Affairs Minister Le Hoai Trung, with the two sides discussing ways to commemorate the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between India and Vietnam in 2027.
The embassy said the anniversary would be marked in the spirit of the Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu LIVE updates: No loss of life in Andhra Pradesh due to Cyclone Murasu, says NDRF
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Cyclone is expected to subside into a deep depression by Tuesday (November 3, 2026) midnight with wind speeds reaching up to 75 kmph

In an effort to provide swift assistance to citizens affected by Cyclone Murasu, the Andhra Pradesh government’s Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) has rolled out a dedicated grievance reporting mechanism through its ‘Mana Mitra’ WhatsApp Governance platform, an official release said on Monday.

Residents in cyclone-hit regions can report emergencies and civic disruptions—such as power outages, uprooted trees, collapsed walls, waterlogging, and other distress situations—by sending a message to the dedicated WhatsApp number 9552300009.

The facility is designed to establish direct communication between citizens and administration, enabling prompt on-ground intervention and effective coordination during disaster management operations.

According to officials, citizens can report cyclone-related grievances by following a simple step-by-step process: Send a “Hi” to WhatsApp number 9552300009. Select the “Services” option from the menu. Choose “Murasu Cyclone Issues”. Click on “Report Issue” and confirm. - ANI
Hand-in-hand with emergency crews, our army of government officials is facing the full brunt of #CycloneMurasu to keep Andhra Pradesh safe.
No casualties have been recorded in Andhra Pradesh till now due to Cyclone Murasu, the NDRF said.

The federal contingency force has deployed 14 teams in the coastal State that has been the “most affected” by the cyclone, Mohsen Shahedi, DIG, National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), told reporters at a press briefing.

Severe cyclonic storm Murasu has made landfall near Ongole, South Andhra Pradesh bringing torrential rain and gale-force winds up to 100 kmph across the region. The severe weather system has severely disrupted normal life in Prakasam district and surrounding areas.

To ensure passenger safety and safe train operations, the Vijayawada Division of South Coast Railway has suspended train movements on the Vijayawada-Ongole-Gudur section until further notice. Passengers planning to travel through these routes are stritly advised to verify running status on official channels such as NTES app. -- The Hindu Bureau

Three districts in Telangana were placed under red alert — indicating possibility of extremely heavy rain — on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), under the impact of the severe cyclonic storm Murasu (war drum). The eye of the storm crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast at 5.30 a.m.

While Nalgonda and Nagakurnool were earlier placed under the weather alert, India Meteorological Department-Hyderabad Centre on Tuesday has forecast extremely heavy rain in Suryapet, Khammam and Bhadradri Kothagudem districts. -- The Hindu Bureau

Naguluppalapadu mandal in Prakasam district recorded the highest rainfall of 198 mm in the 24 hours ending at 8.30 a.m. on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), as Cyclone Murasu brought heavy to very heavy rainfall across several parts of the district. Kothapatnam mandal followed with 182.3 mm, while Ongole Urban recorded 174.7 mm during the same period. The cyclone hit near Kothapatnam beach on the shore of Bay of Bengal.

articles.title: Poultry industry pushes for ₹110 per kg live chicken price
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The challenges posed by rising maize prices amid shortages in availability attributed to the impact of El Niño conditions was discussed at a meeting held in Hyderabad

Concerned over recent fluctuations in broiler chicken prices and rising input costs, poultry industry leaders from across the country have called for coordinated efforts to stabilise the market and maintain a benchmark price of ₹110 per kg for live chicken.

The decision was taken at a high-level meeting held in Hyderabad on Monday (November 2, 2026), where representatives of the All India Poultry Breeders Association (AIPBA), Pan India Breeders Coordination Committee (PIBCC) and several State poultry associations discussed the challenges confronting the poultry sector.

Industry leaders observed that the recent decline in chicken prices was largely seasonal, coinciding with reduced consumption during the festival period, and urged stakeholders not to panic. They resolved to meet government representatives and policymakers in New Delhi next week to discuss these issues and other pressing challenges facing the poultry industry.

The leaders emphasised the need for policy interventions to address rising feed costs, particularly by facilitating duty-free imports of non-genetically modified (non-GMO) maize. Highlighting the abundant availability of soybean in the market, the participants urged poultry farmers and other stakeholders not to panic over the recent price fluctuations, which they described as temporary.

The challenges posed by rising maize prices amid shortages in availability attributed to the impact of El Niño conditions and their impact on poultry production costs were discussed at the meeting. Industry representatives stressed the need for collective efforts to ensure price stability and protect the interests of poultry farmers and other stakeholders.
AIPBA chairman Bahadur Ali, PIBCC convenor Vasanth Kumar Shetty, Telangana Poultry Breeders Association (TPBA) president A. Tirupathi Reddy and other industry representatives attended the meeting.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: floodwater recedes, but damaged roads remain a concern in Chennai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chennai recorded an average of 2.08 mm rain between 6 a.m. and 2 p.m. During this eight-hour period, 47 stations recorded very light rain and 16 recorded light rain. Ennore recorded the highest rainfall at 5.6 mm.

As cyclone Murasu brought overnight rains lashing the city from Sunday (November 1, 2026) night, rainwater stagnation reported in several parts of Chennai had receded by 11 a.m. on Monday (November 2). However, damaged roads, potholes and stretches left uneven after stormwater drain and utility works continued to trouble residents and councillors of Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC). they urged the civic body to rectify problems before next rains due to Northeast monsoon hit the city in December.

According to Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC) of GCC, Chennai recorded an average rainfall of 76.07 mm in the 24 hours ending at 6 a.m. on November 2, according to data from the Greater Chennai Corporation’s Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC). Of the monitoring stations, 28 recorded heavy rain and five recorded very heavy rain. Parrys recorded the highest rainfall at 149.2 mm, followed by New Manali Town at 141.6 mm.

Rainfall intensity eased considerably on November 2. The city recorded an average of 2.08 mm between 6 a.m. and 2 p.m. During this eight-hour period, 47 stations recorded very light rain and 16 recorded light rain. Ennore recorded the highest rainfall at 5.6 mm.

Ambedkar Valavan aka Kumarasamy, VCK party councillor of Purasaiwalkam, said there was no water stagnation in his ward, including Thideer Nagar and Periyar Nagar. He said earlier works had addressed the waterlogging problems reported in the area. However, he flagged the poor condition of several roads, including Rettamalai Srinivasan Salai and Cooks Road, from Otteri Bridge towards Binny Mills, where potholes and uneven surfaces remained.

Following the rains from Cyclone Murasu, stagnant rainwater was being drained at Sai Nagar 9th Cross Street in Thoraipakkam under Sholinganallur Zone by Greater Chennai Corporation on November 2, 2026. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

He said several roads in Thiru.Vi.Ka Nagar Zone, including New Barren Road, Kunnur High Road, Strahans Road, Perambur Barracks Road, Ganeshapuram Road, Ambedkar College Road and Basin Bridge Road, had been affected by excavation works for Metro Rail and Metro Water projects. Sections had been dug up and left uneven without proper restoration, he said. Even light rain could make such stretches hazardous for motorists, particularly those unfamiliar with the road conditions.

He also flagged the continued closure of the Ganeshapuram subway despite the road work not progressing. The closure had forced residents of surrounding neighbourhoods to take longer routes to reach cremation grounds. Residents who could earlier reach the B.B. Road crematorium after travelling about half a kilometre now had to travel nearly eight km, he said.

Following the rains from Cyclone Murasu, repair work is underway to fix potholes formed on the road at Ponniamman Koil Street near Manjambakkam under Manali Zone by the Greater Chennai Corporation on November 2, 2026. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Mr. Kumarasamy alleged that road works awarded during the previous regime had been stopped after the change of government, with officials citing a lack of funds. He said estimates and repair works had not been prepared in advance of the monsoon. He also criticised the absence of advance arrangements such as deploying tractors, generators and pumps in vulnerable locations.

Chennai recorded an average of 2.08 mm rain between 6 a.m. and 2 p.m. During this eight-hour period, 47 stations recorded very light rain and 16 recorded light rain. Ennore recorded the highest rainfall at 5.6 mm.

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: ISRO needs more human and material resources to fulfil its mandate

With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

articles.title: Dwindling support: On the U.S. and the Cuban embargo
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India and the world must stand up against the bullying of Cuba by the U.S.

Nearly every year since 1992, the United Nations General Assembly has passed a resolution calling on the U.S. to end its decades-old economic embargo on Cuba . As a result, the outcome at the UNGA resolution titled the ‘Necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba’ passed on October 30, was expected. Surprisingly, the support for the resolution this year was dramatically lower than previous years. For the preceding decade, more than 180 countries of the 193-member UNGA had expressed their support for ending the embargo, but the numbers dropped to 165 in favour in 2025; this year’s tally dropped sharply lower, with 130 in favour, 25 abstaining and 17 countries voting against the resolution. The trend clearly points to efforts by the Trump administration to use its pressure on countries to change their votes, and many appear to have succumbed to those threats. Among those were several Latin American countries, that have more recently grown closer to the U.S., particularly after the operation in Venezuela in January 2026 , where U.S. marines abducted President Maduro and brought him to the U.S. for a trial. Countries in the region such as Costa Rica, Ecuador, Argentina, and Colombia that have downgraded ties with Havana, switched votes on the resolution. In addition, U.S. diplomats argued that Havana-Moscow ties emboldened Russia’s war in Ukraine , which led to several western countries switching their vote. Diplomats from Ukraine and Poland, for example, referred to Cuba’s ties with Russia while explaining their vote, and Germany and Italy switched for the first time in many years to abstaining on the resolution. While it is clear that the bulk of the Group of 77 and non-aligned states including India maintained their support on the resolution for Cuba, the vote by the others demonstrates a disquieting turn.

Amidst these turns, New Delhi must be credited for standing firm on the issue , opposing the embargo, and calling for “dialogue and diplomacy” in its statement. The vote came a month after the BRICS New Delhi declaration expressed “deep concern” over the tightening of unilateral blockade measures on Cuba, and the “worrying humanitarian impact” on the Cuban people. It is important that India continue to stand up to such unilateral measures and amplify the voice of smaller countries, particularly those in the Global South.

articles.title: Open to investigation: On the challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Public functionaries must not use privacy to seek exemption from scrutiny

The Digital News Publishers Association’s (DNPA) challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 , and its Rules , has drawn attention to concerns that a law to safeguard informational privacy risks creating a serious chilling effect on the media. The absence of a specific exemption for journalistic activity could subject reporters investigating official misconduct or corruption to the obligations of a “data fiduciary”, requiring them to notify and seek consent from the very individuals they are investigating. Such onerous requirements could affect investigations undertaken in the public interest. The implications extend to routine newsgathering too, where personal information is integral to reporting. The omission is particularly consequential because the drafts in 2018, 2019 and 2021 carried a journalistic exemption. The Act already provides exemptions for certain forms of data processing, including for research and statistical purposes, making the denial of similar protection to journalists difficult to justify. Non-compliance can attract penalties of up to ₹250 crore, posing an existential threat to smaller and independent newsrooms. The DNPA petition also challenges Section 44(3), which amended the RTI Act, 2005, removing the earlier public-interest qualification concerning disclosure of personal information. The protection of personal information must not be absolute; an overriding public interest must remain a legitimate ground for disclosure, particularly when the information is held by public authorities. Investigations into corruption often rely on asset disclosures and tender documents containing personal data. Restricting access to these records risks reducing journalism to merely reproducing government releases.

The Supreme Court, while issuing notice on the petition, rightly emphasised the need to balance press freedom with the right to privacy. Although journalists in India enjoy no specific statutory protection for their work, freedom of the press is constitutionally protected under Article 19(1)(a). The Court has also shielded newspapers from arbitrary state restrictions. However, growing mistrust of legacy media and the rise of independent content creators have made it difficult to determine who receives such protection. The Centre has also flagged this concern. Yet, carving out distinct categories is no easy task — a 2026 Reuters Institute report shows that the proportion of 18- to 24-year-olds identifying social media as their primary source of news rose from 21% in 2015 to 39% in 2025. A purely legalistic determination of these competing concerns may perhaps prove too onerous. Stakeholders must build consensus on a mutually acceptable framework where public functionaries and those handling public funds are not insulated from scrutiny under the guise of privacy. Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw’s indication that he would meet editors is a welcome step towards consensus.

articles.title: Deemed ineligible: On the Supreme Court and SIR
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court has pointed to the SIR’s flaws by design

At Wednesday’s hearing of a petition on the Delhi SIR in the Supreme Court, Justice Joymalya Bagchi asked questions that cut to the heart of the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s SIR of electoral rolls . If an existing voter was “lax, inert or did not respond” to enumeration forms, was that a ground for the ECI to “forfeit his or her right to vote forever”? The Bench headed by the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said that the ECI was in “error” to force such voters, struck off for not returning enumeration forms, to reapply on Form 6 as if they were new voters. It asked why voters who had shifted residences could not just disclose details and why deleted voters could not fill enumeration forms belatedly. This is the central design flaw of the SIR as it shifts the burden of enrolment from the state to the elector, including those who have voted before, and treats a mere change of address as ground for deletion. The share of draft deletions recorded as “shifted” or “absent” rose from 55% in Bihar to 72% in States/Union Territories in Phase 3. In Karnataka, about 84 lakh electors were deleted, marked as “shifted” or “absent” during enumeration. But only a net of 8.2 lakh, including new electors, were added during the claims phase, with the final roll being 64.5 lakh short of the projected adult population. Requiring moved voters to re-register as fresh applicants defeats the ECI’s historic mandate of widening the franchise, which was inherent in the 2002-03 intensive revision, where enumerators enrolled shifted voters at their new homes and the Chief Electoral Officer reconciled the old entries.

Justice Bagchi also mentioned that the Bihar judgment was not a “binding precedent” and that the legality of “logical discrepancy” checks, allowed only as an “interim arrangement” in West Bengal, had not been finally adjudicated. No statute or rule provides for judging a voter’s eligibility on the basis of family size or the age gap between voters and parents, which were two of the ECI’s ludicrous and algorithm-driven “logical discrepancy” checks. In West Bengal these checks resulted in massive disenfranchisement and The Hindu’s analysis found that in Delhi, Muslims were disproportionately flagged. But the Court should not merely issue managerial fixes such as extended deadlines or displaying printed lists in blocks, as it has in the past. The final SIR rolls are erroneous as deletions flowed from a flawed design rather than just lapses by the ECI. The dead and duplicate entries that the SIR identified should be removed and newly eligible electors added. Voters wrongly removed from draft rolls must be included again. The larger questions over the Commission’s SIR conduct and how its members are appointed must also be settled.

articles.title: Even as unemployment falls, lack of ‘decent work’ in India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Poor-quality employment generation has consequences for economic growth; workers without social security spend less, save less and remain vulnerable to economic shocks

I ndia’s unemployment rate fell from 6.1% in 2017-18 to 3.2% in 2023-24. At the same time, female workforce participation increased for the first time in decades as has been widely reported in government documents. In light of these positive developments, it is the right time to ask what kind of jobs have been generated in India recently, and what working conditions accompany them.

This is important because employment alone does not inherently ensure dignity, security, or a stable livelihood. A worker engaged in garment sewing without a formal contract, a gig worker without insurance coverage, or a construction labourer without paid leave may technically be considered employed, but they remain outside the promise of decent work. The International Labour Organization (ILO) defines ‘decent work’ as employment that offers equitable income, workplace rights, social security and dignity. This principle is integrated into Sustainable Development Goal 8 (SDG-8), which advocates “decent work for all”. Measured this way, India’s labour market persistently exhibits high levels of informality, insecure employment, and increasing inequalities.

Using two rounds of the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), 2017-18 and 2023-24, the quality of employment in India has been analysed. By constructing a multidimensional Decent Work Index (DWI) based on three subdimensions — employment status, employment opportunity, and social security — across five major industries (agriculture, manufacturing, construction, wholesale and retail, and transport), it was observed that India has made progress in improving work conditions over time. The overall DWI increased from 0.247 in 2017-18 to 0.302 in 2023-24. While this indicates some improvement in job quality, the overall level remains alarmingly low. More importantly, progress has been uneven across sectors, regions, gender and caste groups.

Manufacturing in the secondary sector and transport in the tertiary sector showed the highest improvement in decent work conditions during this period. The manufacturing sector’s DWI increased from 0.324 to 0.411 due to a gradual rise in formalisation and digitalisation. The transport sector also experienced significant progress (from 0.285 to 0.35), largely due to the expansion of urban logistics and app-based platform work.

However, these improvements also reveal an important concern. Even in sectors where employment conditions have improved, access to social security remains limited. A large number of workers still do not have written contracts, paid leave, provident fund benefits or insurance coverage. Though employment opportunities are increasing, labour protections and job security are not improving at the same pace. Agriculture, which continues to employ the largest share of India’s workforce, remains the lowest-quality employment generating sector. The agricultural sector’s DWI marginally increased from 0.211 to 0.267 during the study period; most agricultural workers continue to be self-employed or unpaid family workers without stable income or labour protections. The issue is not merely low productivity; rather it is the rise of informal jobs. Construction and retail sectors tell a similar story. Workers remain dependent on casual employment, subcontracting chains and insecure labour arrangements. Welfare schemes exist on paper but implementation gaps continue to exclude millions of workers.

Nearly 90% of India’s workforce remains informally employed, a share that has risen since 2019, according to the India Employment Report 2024 (ILO–IHD). articles.title: Cyclone Murasu LIVE update: Orange alert in six Telangana districts, yellow alert in five; holiday announced for schools, colleges in T.N., A.P. districts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The cyclonic storm lay centred about 350 km east of Chennai, 400 km east-southeast of Nellore, 430 km southeast of Machilipatnam, 420 km east-southeast of Kavali, 450 km southeast of Ongole, and 520 km south of Visakhapatnam, according to IMD.
Chennai District Collector S. Malathi Helen and Tiruvallur District Collector S. Kavitha last night announced a holiday for schools and colleges on Monday.

According to data from the Regional Meteorological Centre here, till 10.30 p.m. on Sunday, in Chennai district, the Nungambakkam station recorded 20.4 mm of rainfall, Meenambakkam recorded 4.9 mm, YMCA Nandanam recorded 13.5 mm, Ennore Port 39 mm, Madhavaram 21 mm, Anna University 10.5 mm and Taramani 7.5 mm.
In Tiruvallur district, Puzhal recorded 11 mm, Poonamallee 0.5 mm, and in Chengalpattu district, VIT Chennai recorded 0.5 mm of rainfall.

In the wake of the cyclone, Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu today called Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to seek assistance from the T.N. government for the restoration of power systems, according to the A.P. CM office.
Mr. Naidu requested that manpower and machinery be sent for restoration, as a large number of power poles were damaged due to the Murasu cyclone.
Mr. Vijay has reportedly responded positively to the request.
Palnadu District Collector Kritika Shukla has announced holiday for all government and private schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres on Tuesday (November 2) in view of Cyclone Murasu.

articles.title: Rebel leaders of AIADMK do not take part in district secretaries’ meeting chaired by Palaniswami
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The party’s performance in the recent bypoll in Dharapuram and Madurantakam Assembly constituencies, and preparations for its general council and executive committee meetings, expected to be conducted in December this year, were among the issues discussed at the meeting

The rebel leaders in the AIADMK, S.P. Velumani and Natham R. Viswanathan, did not take part in the meeting of party’s district secretaries chaired by general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami at the party head office in Chennai on Sunday.

The party’s performance in the recent bypoll in Dharapuram and Madurantakam Assembly constituencies, and preparations for its general council and executive committee meetings, expected to be conducted in December this year, were among the issues discussed at the meeting. Senior leaders A. Tamilmagan Hussain, K.P. Munusamy, and Dindigul C. Sreenivasan were among those who attended the meeting.

Earlier, Mr. Palaniswami issued a statement criticising the TVK-led government over the rates of medicines in Mudhalvar Marundhagams (formerly Amma Marundhagams). Citing a report from the All India Drug Action Network, he said medicines at Amma Marundhagams were being sold at rates higher than the prices fixed, which is affecting the poor.
Retired Additional Superintendent of Police S. Velladurai, who was known for his involvement in many ‘police encounter’ cases, joined the AIADMK in the presence of Mr. Palaniswami on Sunday.

articles.title: Litigants will not be entitled to refund of court fees if disputes get settled out of court after commencement of trial, rules Madras High Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice P.B. Balaji refuses to follow Supreme Court’s 2017 verdict in M.C. Subramaniam’s case and instead follows the top court’s 2010 judgment in Afcons Infrastructure case

Litigants will not be entitled to return of court fees if their civil disputes lead to an out of the court settlement after the commencement of trial in civil suits, the Madras High Court has held after refusing to follow the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the 2021 M.C. Subramaniam’s case.

Justice P.B. Balaji agreed with Advocate General (A-G) Vijay Narayan that the 2021 verdict in M.C. Subramaniam’s case had not factored in the top court’s 2010 judgement passed by a bench of co-equal strength in Afcons Infrastruture Limited versus Cherian Varkey Construction Company Private Limited.

“It is settled law that when there is an earlier ratio of a Coordinate Bench, it is binding on a later Bench of equal strength and if at all the later Bench is not agreeable to the ratio laid down in the earlier decision, it is only open to the later Bench to refer the matter to a larger Bench and not take a contrary view,” the judge said.
He went on to state: “In such view of the matter, I am emboldened to follow and rely upon the ratio laid down in Afcons case instead of following the ratio laid down in M.C.Subramaniam’s case.”

The judge said, the Tamil Nadu Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1955 insists upon litigants to pay court fees for a reason. The court fee gets collected to meet all necessary and incidental expenses relating to provision of infrastructure for courts, conduct of trials, payment of salaries and allowances to the court staff and so on.

Section 69 of the 1955 Act, as it stood originally, provided for refund of 50% of court fees “whenever any suit is dismissed as settled out of court before any evidence has been recorded on the merits of the claim.” In 2007, Section 69A was introduced to the Act providing for refund of 100% of the court fees if the dispute gets settled after the court concerned refers the matter for arbitration, mediation, conciliation, Lok Adalat or such other alternative dispute resolution (ADR) mechanisms mentioned in Section 89 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC).

In 2017, the Act was amended again to provide for return of 100% court fees under Section 69 too. However, even then, the legislature consciously did not tinker with the words “whenever any suit is dismissed as settled out of court before any evidence has been recorded on the merits of the claim.”

Further, Justice Balaji highlighted that the Supreme Court in Afcons Infrastructure case had held that the civil courts could refer disputes to the ADR mechanisms mentioned in Section 89 of CPC only before commencement of trial because otherwise, the litigants could use it as a ruse to protract the trial.

Therefore, the continued existence of Section 69 along with the words “before any evidence has been recorded on the merits of the claim” and the Supreme Court’s 2010 ruling that courts could refer civil disputes for ADR only before commencement of trial would make it clear that litigants would not be entitled to refund of court fees after the trial commences, the judge held.

The verdict was passed while dismissing two civil revision petitions filed by different litigants. The first civil revision petition had been filed against the order passed by a district court in Tiruvallur district to refund only 50% of court fees and the second had been filed against Chengalpattu court’s order that the litigant would not be entitled to refund of the entire amount of ₹2.54 lakh paid towards court fees.

Justice Balaji held that both the petitioners would not be entitled to refund of any amount of court fees since the out of court settlement had been reached only after commencement of trial. However, since the State had not filed any revision petition against the order to refund 50% of court fees to the first petitioner, the judge refrained from interfering with the Tiruvallur court’s order.

The judge had requested the A-G to assist him in the case considering the important question of law involved in the case related to the State exchequer and recorded the court’s “deep appreciations” to him. He also appreciated senior counsel S. Parthasarathy and S. Subbiah, amicus curiae S. Suresh Sampath, advocates S. Ramesh, S.R. Sundar, A.V. Arun and all other Bar members who made their submissions following an open invitation extended to all of them.

Section 69 of the 1955 Act, as it stood originally, provided for refund of 50% of court fees “whenever any suit is dismissed as settled out of court before any evidence has been recorded on the merits of the claim.” In 2007, Section 69A was introduced to the Act providing for refund of 100% of the court fees if the dispute gets settled after the court concerned refers the matter for arbitration, mediation, conciliation, Lok Adalat or such other alternative dispute resolution (ADR) mechanisms mentioned in Section 89 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC).

In 2017, the Act was amended again to provide for return of 100% court fees under Section 69 too. However, even then, the legislature consciously did not tinker with the words “whenever any suit is dismissed as settled out of court before any evidence has been recorded on the merits of the claim.”

Further, Justice Balaji highlighted that the Supreme Court in Afcons Infrastructure case had held that the civil courts could refer disputes to the ADR mechanisms mentioned in Section 89 of CPC only before commencement of trial because otherwise, the litigants could use it as a ruse to protract the trial.

Therefore, the continued existence of Section 69 along with the words “before any evidence has been recorded on the merits of the claim” and the Supreme Court’s 2010 ruling that courts could refer civil disputes for ADR only before commencement of trial would make it clear that litigants would not be entitled to refund of court fees after the trial commences, the judge held.

The verdict was passed while dismissing two civil revision petitions filed by different litigants. The first civil revision petition had been filed against the order passed by a district court in Tiruvallur district to refund only 50% of court fees and the second had been filed against Chengalpattu court’s order that the litigant would not be entitled to refund of the entire amount of ₹2.54 lakh paid towards court fees.

Justice Balaji held that both the petitioners would not be entitled to refund of any amount of court fees since the out of court settlement had been reached only after commencement of trial. However, since the State had not filed any revision petition against the order to refund 50% of court fees to the first petitioner, the judge refrained from interfering with the Tiruvallur court’s order.

The judge had requested the A-G to assist him in the case considering the important question of law involved in the case related to the State exchequer and recorded the court’s “deep appreciations” to him. He also appreciated senior counsel S. Parthasarathy and S. Subbiah, amicus curiae S. Suresh Sampath, advocates S. Ramesh, S.R. Sundar, A.V. Arun and all other Bar members who made their submissions following an open invitation extended to all of them.

1. Core Context & Background: Justice P.B. Balaji refuses to follow Supreme Court’s 2017 verdict in M.C. Subramaniam’s case and instead follows the top court’s 2010 judgment in Afcons Infrastructure case

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Litigants will not be entitled to return of court fees if their civil disputes lead to an out of the court settlement after the commencement of trial in civil suits, the Madras High Court has held after refusing to follow the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the 2021 M.C. Subramaniam’s case.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The judge had requested the A-G to assist him in the case considering the important question of law involved in the case related to the State exchequer and recorded the court’s “deep appreciations” to him. He also appreciated senior counsel S. Parthasarathy and S. Subbiah, amicus curiae S. Suresh Sampath, advocates S. Ramesh, S.R. Sundar, A.V. Arun and all other Bar members who made their submissions following an open invitation extended to all of them.

articles.title: BJP alleges rift between Rahul, Priyanka; accuses LoP of sidelining sister at INDIA bloc protests
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘Yesterday, during the mock Parliament organised by the Congress party and led by Rahul Gandhi, I observed one thing: Priyanka Vadra was not given an opportunity to speak by Rahul Gandhi or the Congress party,’ said Sambit Patra

The BJP on Sunday (November 1, 2026) claimed the Congress has split into two camps led by Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, and that she was not "allowed" to speak at the two INDIA bloc protests as the Leader of Opposition feared getting sidelined by his sister.

In a video message on Instagram, BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra said Priyanka Gandhi's "vote has also been stolen" within the Gandhi family and claimed she appeared unhappy at the mock parliament and the Ramlila Maidan rally.

The INDIA bloc on Saturday (October 31, 2026) held a symbolic "public impeachment" of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that the right to vote was under threat as the poll panel was functioning at the behest of the Modi government.
On Sunday (November 1, 2026), the Opposition grouping held a mammoth rally at Ramlila Maidan here against alleged electoral irregularities and voter list revision.

"Yesterday, during the mock Parliament organised by the Congress party and led by Rahul Gandhi, I observed one thing: Priyanka Vadra was not given an opportunity to speak by Rahul Gandhi or the Congress party," Patra said.
Everyone, including non-parliamentarians, was given an opportunity to speak, he said.

"Today, at the rally at Ramlila Maidan, too, everyone expressed their views and spoke on their respective issues. But Priyanka Vadra appeared unhappy even today. Once again, she was not given an opportunity to speak," he said.
"Could it be that a political game is being played within the Gandhi family itself?

"Could it be that Rahul Gandhi fears that if Priyanka Vadra is projected as a leader, he might be sidelined? Is this why Priyanka Vadra's vote has also been stolen within the Gandhi family?" the BJP leader asked.

BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari wondered whether Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi camps had emerged within the Congress and accused the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha of suppressing the rise of his sister.
"Is a Rahul camp versus Priyanka camp emerging within the Congress party? Is the country now witnessing the battle between Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Vadra unfold in the open?" he asked.

"Today, at Ramlila Maidan, Priyanka Vadra was not allowed to speak. Priyanka, who has served as the Congress party's general secretary and is Rahul Gandhi's sister, was not given an opportunity to address the gathering by Rahul Gandhi," he said.

articles.title: NTK cadre want Seeman to seek AIADMK, DMK support for Ambasamudram byelection
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: His decision to contest is being seen as ‘bold’ and has reportedly energised the cadre after a disappointing showing in this year’s Assembly elections

NTK chief coordinator Seeman’s decision to contest in the Ambasamudram Assembly bypoll (when notified) has set off a debate among the party’s senior office-bearers whether it should seek the support of the DMK and the AIADMK for fielding him as the “common candidate”.

A senior party office-bearer said Mr. Seeman had been facing “pressure” internally to reach out to the leadership of the DMK and the AIADMK and ask for support. “Though it is a longshot, our office-bearers are putting pressure on him to reach out to the other parties. Mr. Seeman has explained to them that such a move would go against the fundamental position of the NTK,” an office-bearer said.

Mr. Seeman’s decision to contest was being seen as “bold” and had reportedly energised the cadre after a disappointing showing in this year’s Assembly elections, which saw its vote share reduce by almost half — falling from 8% to around 4%.
Mr. Seeman is yet to win an election despite trying his luck since 2016. A senior member of the party said: “Only a leader who takes these risky moves can keep the party and its cadre with him.”

Regarding the possibility of a common candidate, a party leader admitted it may not “possible” given the current political dynamics in the State. “Our decision to announce that Seeman will contest has given rise to these speculations,” he said.
Party sources said while Mr. Seeman would not formally seek the support of the DMK and the AIADMK, he would nevertheless welcome if “they not contest the elections”.

articles.title: U.S. mid-term elections: How officials are facing the heat
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Poor-quality employment generation has consequences for economic growth; workers without social security spend less, save less and remain vulnerable to economic shocks

A mericans vote tomorrow, November 3, to elect the Congress for the last two years of Donald Trump’s presidency. While Indian voters are used to a single counting day, with most results in by evening, a U.S. count can run for days, and in a close race for weeks. This year the worry is whether the outcome will be accepted at all. In 2020, doubts arose after the count, and Mr. Trump still has not accepted that defeat. This time, they are being raised before voting, with Mr. Trump stating that he will accept the result only “if the elections are honest”.

The U.S. does have a federal Election Assistance Commission (EAC), but its responsibility is limited to certifying voting machines and training election staff. The 50 States have thousands of county officials who man the booths, count the votes and declare results; India’s electronic voting machines can total crores of votes in a few hours. In the U.S., many votes come by post, and each envelope must be opened and its signature checked before the ballot is counted. Moreover, there is variance in the procedure followed by different States. California will accept a postal ballot up to a week after polling day if it was posted in time. Twenty-six States order an automatic recount when the margin is very narrow.

Global & Diplomatic Brief: U.S. mid-term elections: How officials are facing the heat. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and proactive engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

Geopolitical Significance: Strengthening strategic partnerships across the Indo-Pacific, Global South, and multilateral forums such as the UN, G20, BRICS, and SCO remains central to India's foreign policy.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu LIVE updates: Odisha expedites evacuation from vulnerable areas as storm intensifies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: System intensifies into ‘Severe Cyclonic Storm’, likely to cross the south Andhra coast, between 11.30 p.m. today and 4 a.m. on November 3.
The Odisha government on Monday (November 2, 2026) expedited the evacuation of people from vulnerable areas.

Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said southern districts Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri were on high alert, with more than 300 NDRF, ODRAF and Fire Service teams pre-positioned. Heavy rain with gusty winds of 40-50 kmph is forecast for parts of Gajapati and Ganjam.

Chennai International Airport, in a post on social media platform X, said eleven flights have been cancelled to and from Chennai owing to the Cyclone. IndiGo has also confirmed in a post on X that “flight operations to and from Rajahmundry, Vijayawada and Tirupati are impacted.”

Ten IndiGo flights scheduled from Gannavaram Airport today (November 2, 2026) were cancelled, affecting passengers travelling to and from Vijayawada. Passengers have been advised to check flight status with the airline before heading to the airport.
A total of eleven flights arriving and departing from Chennai airport has been cancelled due to cyclone Murasu on Monday (November 2, 2026).
In a statement, Airports Authority of India (AAI) said, flights to and from destinations including Vijayawada, Kadapa, Rajahmundry and Tiruchi will be cancelled.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said severe cyclonic storm ‘Murasu’ lay over the west-central Bay of Bengal at 8.30 a.m. IST today (November 2, 2026), about 160 km east-southeast of Nellore and 180 km northeast of Chennai, moving west-northwestwards at 22 kmph.

It is very likely to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast, between Nellore and Narsapur and south of Ongole, between 11.30 p.m. today and 4 a.m. on November 3, with winds of 100-110 kmph gusting to 120 kmph.

Northern Tamil Nadu received heavy rain, and several places in Chennai were inundated, as Cyclone Murasu lay about 250-260 km from Chennai, heading for landfall over south coastal Andhra Pradesh. Chennai, Chengalpattu and Tiruvallur have had torrential rain since Sunday night, with Madhavaram recording 11 cm, and Ennore Port and Nungambakkam 10 cm each over 24 hours.

The IMD has issued an orange alert for Chennai, and schools in the city have a holiday today (November 2, 2026). Chennai Airport authorities said certain flights have been cancelled, and passengers have been asked to contact their airlines.

Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu was centred about 180 km north-east of Chennai and 160 km east-south-east of Nellore at 8.30 a.m. on Monday (November 2, 2026), the IMD said in a post on X. It is very likely to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, south of Ongole, from 11.30 p.m. on Monday to 4 a.m. on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).
Wind speeds of 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph, are expected at landfall.
