articles.title: Deepavali sales expected to gain momentum in Coimbatore next week
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: With Deepavali falling in the first week of a month this year, people are likely to begin shopping after receiving their monthly salaries and festival bonuses; the last 5-6 days preceding the festival is likely to witness massive retail activity
Shopping for the Deepavali festival in Coimbatore city this year is expected to pick up next week across sectors.
President of the Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Coimbatore, C. Dorairaj, told The Hindu on Thursday (October 29) that several companies in Coimbatore will disburse bonuses next week.

With the festival coming in the first week of a month this year, people are likely to start purchases after getting the monthly salary and the festival bonus. So, the last 5-6 days preceding the festival is expected to see huge retail activity.
Be it textiles, FMCG, or household appliances, the retailers are expecting good sales this year.

All the products have seen a price hike, ranging between 10% and 30%, in the last few months, depending on the product. So, the retailers may see higher revenue though the volume of sales may remain the same as last year or slightly better in some sectors, he added.

In the case of textiles, while the large, multi brand retail outlets are already witnessing a pick up of sales, the smaller outlets are facing stiff competition from online sellers. Further, business at the small retail shops will go up in the last few days before the festival.

Though gold and silver prices saw a decline recently, jewellery retailers are yet to see business picking up. “We were hoping for better sales as the prices fell. But, consumers are waiting for further fall in prices,” said B. Sabarinath, president of the Coimbatore Jewellers Association.
The household appliances outlets are also expecting better sales only from next week.
In the case of sweets and savouries, most of the bulk buyers will purchase products for distribution just days before the festival, Mr. Dorairaj said.

articles.title: Rubio says U.S. not directly involved in Flavio Bolsonaro’s flight from Brazil
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Bolsonaro, who lost his bid to be president in the October 25 run-off vote, arrived with his family in the U.S. on October 28
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday (October 31, 2026) that Washington was not directly involved in Flavio Bolsonaro’s arrangements to leave Brazil after his election loss.

Mr. Bolsonaro, who lost his bid to be president in Sunday’s (October 25, 2026) run-off vote, arrived with his family in the U.S. on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) after a court ordered his passports be seized amid multiple investigations against him.

“He had previously held a visa, and the President made a decision to allow him to enter the country,” Mr. Rubio told a press conference in Atlanta, Georgia, where he hosted G20 Foreign Ministers for a two-day meeting.
But Mr. Rubio added that “the U.S. government was not involved directly” in arrangements Mr. Bolsonaro made to leave his country.

Following the vote, the 45-year-old bolted from Brazil via Argentina and Ecuador in a plane that some U.S. media, including The New York Times and The Wall Street Journa l, reported was chartered by Jason Miller, an adviser to U.S. President Donald Trump.
The plane that whisked the Mr. Bolsonaro family to the United States was paid for by an intermediary from a U.S. bank account, the head of the airline has told AFP .
The White House has not commented on the flight, but Mr. Trump has called the Brazilian election “disgraceful.”

A Brazilian diplomatic source, speaking on condition of anonymity, told AFP that Argentina’s diplomatic representative had been summoned for a “routine meeting” to “provide explanations” on the flight.
Argentina’s Foreign Minister later denied that Brazil had asked Buenos Aires to explain its role in the operation.
Since arriving in the U.S., Mr. Bolsonaro has claimed to be the true leader of Brazil and said that he left the country because he was a victim of “persecution.”
Flavio Bolsonaro’s father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, is serving a 27-year sentence under house arrest for plotting a coup after his 2022 re-election loss.

articles.title: Andhra civic polls: TDP, YSRCP workers clash in Pulivendula; 22.08% turnout by 11 a.m. | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Fourteen vehicles were set on fire in Pulivendula, Kadapa district, Andhra Pradesh hours before polling began on Sunday

The YSRCP “seems to have come ‘well-prepared’ in Kadapa” while the rest of the State is voting peacefully, Minister Nara Lokesh said in a post on X on Sunday. The election authorities would deal with “criminal elements”, he said, urging voters to turn out in large numbers.

Turnout in Kadapa district’s urban bodies stood at 25.46% by 11 a.m., above the State average of 22.08%, according to the State Election Commission’s figures. Jammalamadugu recorded 60.92% and Pulivendula 35.17%. Kadapa city, the district’s only corporation, was at 18.54%.

YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy accused the State Election Commission of failing to ensure a level playing field in the municipal elections and of siding with the ruling NDA government. Speaking to reporters in Pulivendula on Sunday (November 1, 2026), he said the SEC should give every candidate a fair chance from nominations to counting. “Only then it will be termed as an election,” he said.

He alleged that journalists had been beaten up and their cameras destroyed in Pulivendula. Polling agents were not allowed into polling stations, he claimed. The Centre should step in even though the TDP is its ally, he said. “If today an NDA partner is permitted to do so and the central government chooses to ignore it, then democracy will not prevail.”

Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy flew into Pulivendula by helicopter on Sunday, in what was termed an “emergency landing”. He had reportedly been given permission to arrive on Saturday. The district administration, busy with the polls, had expressed difficulty in providing security.

Former Chief Minister and Pulivendula MLA Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy arrived in his constituency on Sunday morning, while voting was under way in the town’s municipal elections. He reportedly took out a roadshow, which TDP workers objected to. The TDP has accused him of violating the Model Code of Conduct. The YSRCP said he had come to cast his vote and that people walked alongside him in support.

Shaik Dastagiri, an accused-turned-approver in the Y.S. Vivekananda Reddy murder case, confronted Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy’s convoy on a busy road, causing tension. Mr. Dastagiri, known for his rivalry with the Y.S. family, reportedly shouted at him during the brief encounter.

Supporters of YSRCP Mayor candidate Varudu Kalyani got into an argument with TDP workers in Ward 29 of Visakhapatnam’s East Assembly constituency on Sunday. It happened while Ms. Kalyani was returning after casting her vote at a polling station in the area. The police stepped in quickly and asked both groups to leave. - Harish Gilai

About 21.40 lakh of Andhra Pradesh’s 96.89 lakh urban voters had cast their votes by 11 a.m. on Sunday, a turnout of 22.08%, according to the State Election Commission. Smaller towns are well ahead of cities. Jammalamadugu in Kadapa district leads the State at 60.92%, followed by Kuppam at 44.30% and Nagari at 40.46%. In Pulivendula, the scene of clashes this morning, 35.17% had voted.

The 13 municipal corporations are trailing: Chittoor leads them at 32.50%. Vijayawada was at 18.07% and Guntur at 17.82%. Visakhapatnam, the largest, was the lowest at 13.34%. 11 AM- Poll Percentage.pdf

YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy is on a visit to Pulivendula in Kadapa district on Sunday, where municipal polling is under way. The TDP has accused him of taking part in a roadshow in alleged violation of the Model Code of Conduct.​​ ​​

Polling picked up in Visakhapatnam through the morning. Turnout rose from 3.34% at 9 a.m. to 13.34% by 11 a.m. on Sunday, according to election officials. Of the city’s 18.37 lakh voters, 2,45,251 had voted by then.

articles.title: Anantapur chainsaw attack: A.P. Minister Nara Lokesh says Class 10 girl stable after bleeding controlled
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Minister said that the medical team at Manipal Hospital stabilised the girl’s condition with blood transfusions and supportive treatment

The Class 10 student from Zilla Parishad High School in Raptadu, who was attacked with an electric chainsaw on Saturday (October 31, 2026), has been stabilised and receiving significant medical care at Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru.

Andhra Pradesh Education Minister and Human Resources Development Minister Nara Lokesh, who is closely monitoring the situation, updated the victim’s medical condition on X. In the latest post, he said that the medical team at Manipal Hospital stabilised the girl’s condition with blood transfusions and supportive treatment.

“Doctors have successfully controlled the major bleeding in the OT. The child’s BP is now being maintained,” Mr. Lokesh said. He appreciated all the doctors, medical teams and officials who worked tirelessly in coordinating the emergency care.

Update from Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru: The medical team stabilised the condition with blood transfusions and supportive treatment. Doctors have successfully controlled the major bleeding in the OT. The child's BP is now being maintained. Our sincere appreciation to all the doctors, medical teams and officials who worked tirelessly in coordinating the emergency care. The child continues to receive close medical attention. We remain hopeful for a full recovery.
“The child continues to receive close medical attention. We remain hopeful for a full recovery,” he said.
Meanwhile, Mr. Lokesh is likely to reach Bengaluru today to consult the medical team about the girl’s condition and meet the victim’s family to assure them of support for her recovery.

articles.title: Uttarakhand chopper crash: Mortal remains of all six victims recovered, sent to Rishikesh AIIMS
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Officials said that after completing the necessary formalities, the mortal remains were sent to the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Rishikesh, by helicopter

The mortal remains of all six people who died in the helicopter crash near Joshimath in Uttarakhand were recovered and sent to AIIMS, Rishikesh, on Sunday (November 1, 2026) morning, the Chamoli district administration said.
On Friday (October 30), the chopper crashed on a hillside near Chai village in Joshimath while it was returning to Dehradun from the Badrinath shrine.

The mortal remains were brought to the Community Health Centre (CHC), Joshimath, by road. Officials said that after completing the necessary formalities, the mortal remains were sent to the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Rishikesh, by helicopter.

The district administration said that teams of the Indian Army, ITBP, SDRF, NDRF, police, district administration and the Forest Department jointly conducted the search operation amidst challenging conditions in the inaccessible and high-altitude hilly area.
"The bodies of all six deceased were taken out by rescue teams on foot on difficult mountain paths," mentions a statement issued by the district administration on Sunday (November 1).
The operation started on Friday (October 30) after the chopper crashed, but due to the difficult terrain and remote location, it took over 24 hours for teams to complete the operation.

articles.title: ‘Chalo Delhi’ posters dominate as INDIA bloc prepares for mega rally at Ramlila Maidan | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: INDA bloc's 'public impeachment' of CEC Gyanesh Kumar featured accounts from voters who alleged that their names had been deleted from electoral rolls
INDIA bloc leaders and supporters take part in the ‘Chalo Dilli’ march from the Minto Road–Connaught Place junction to Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi on November 1.

The march precedes the Opposition’s mega rally against alleged vote theft and electoral irregularities. The parties are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over concerns surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Tribal communities from across the country performed a cultural dance in Connaught Place ahead of the INDIA bloc’s rally at Ramlila Ground.

Congress leader and Punjab Congress in-charge Sachin Pilot said the government wants to stop people through pressure and prevent them from voicing their opinions, but neither Rahul Gandhi nor “our people” would back down. He said “hundreds of thousands” would arrive from across the country today (November 1, 2026) and that traders would see “a lot of business”.

Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, speaking in Shimla, alleged that Mr. Gandhi was upset because the names of “infiltrators” had been removed through the SIR. He said the BJP stood with the Election Commission. He asked whether the elections in Himachal Pradesh, Kerala and Mr. Gandhi’s own Raebareli seat should be annulled by the same logic, and accused the Congress of “double standards” for claiming votes are “stolen” only where the BJP is in power. He also made an insulting personal remark against Mr. Gandhi.

Mr. Nadda called the Ramlila Maidan rally “a foolish, orchestrated drama”. He alleged that Mr. Gandhi’s politics works in four stages: spreading lies and rumours, inciting street anarchy, damaging the economy, and destabilising an elected government “at the behest of foreign powers”. He said the rally had four aims, among them to “rub salt into the wounds” of Sikhs and to rob Delhi traders of festive-season earnings.
Union Minister J.P. Nadda told Rahul Gandhi that India was “not some ‘banana republic’” where one could “incite arson, trigger riots, or push an agenda for ‘regime change’”.

He called November 1 the “darkest stain” in India’s democratic history, alleging that “goons nurtured by the Congress party” massacred Sikhs on this day in 1984, and said the Gandhi family had never offered a sincere apology. He accused Mr. Gandhi of insensitivity for holding the rally today (November 1, 2026).

Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said the message of the INDIA bloc’s mega protest was “very simple”: “Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao”. He added that it was “not about the Congress” but about the constitutional rights of the Indian people.

CPI(M) MP John Brittas on Sunday (November 1, 2026) described the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan as a landmark protest that would have a major impact on the country’s politics. He claimed that more than 10 lakh people would gather and said the ground was already packed before the event began.

Mr. Brittas said the rally would send a strong message to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah, demanding the immediate removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He warned that the government should act on the demand or face further political consequences.

Congress leader Pawan Khera said “this is the calm before the storm”, adding that the “coming storm will sweep Gyanesh away” and that Amit Shah and Narendra Modi would also “not remain in their positions”.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu to set up 26 POCSO Act courts and four NDPS courts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: With the addition of these POCSO Act courts, there will be 52 special courts across 47 police districts

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has ordered the establishment of 26 courts under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, and four courts under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, to expedite the trial of cases registered under these laws.

A State government press release issued on Sunday (November 1, 2026) said during a review meeting on cases registered under the POCSO Act, the Chief Minister had stressed the need to ensure justice for victims by speeding up trials. He had also sought details on the need for additional courts. Accordingly, the government had decided to establish more courts.

Already, 22 courts dealing with POCSO Act cases and four special courts will start functioning soon. The government said the Chief Minister had ordered the establishment of 12 special courts and 14 additional courts at a cost of ₹46.59 crore, taking into account the volume of cases registered under the Act.

With the addition of these courts, there will be 52 special courts across 47 police districts. They are expected to expedite the delivery of justice and help prevent the recurrence of sexual offences against children, the government said.

The release said, 11 special courts were already functioning to deal with cases registered under the NDPS Act. Four more courts will be established, one each in Kancheepuram, Tiruvallur and Vellore, and an additional court in Chennai.

articles.title: GST mop-up grows 23% to over ₹2.31 lakh cr. in October
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Gross GST collections from domestic sales rose 16% to over ₹1.59 lakh crore, and revenues from imports climbed 42% to ₹72,246 crore

Gross GST collections increased 23% to over ₹2.31 lakh crore in October, driven by strong mop-up from domestic activities and imports, according to government data released on Sunday (November 1, 2026).
Gross GST collections from domestic sales rose 16% to over ₹1.59 lakh crore, and revenues from imports climbed 42% to ₹72,246 crore.
The ₹2.31 lakh crore collection includes Central GST mop-up of ₹42,935 crore, State GST of ₹51,340 crore and Integrated GST of over ₹1.37 lakh crore, data showed.
Goods and Services Tax (GST) refunds increased 6.5% year-on-year to ₹27,934 crore in October.
After adjusting for refunds, net GST collections rose 26% to over ₹2.03 lakh crore in October.
During April-October, gross GST collection grew 13.2% to over ₹14.77 lakh crore. Net collections rose 13% to over ₹12.69 lakh crore.

articles.title: Donald Trump says Flavio Bolsonaro can stay in U.S. as long as he wants amid Brazilian probes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Flavio Bolsonaro’s decision to go to the U.S. followed a ruling by a Brazilian Supreme Court Justice to revoke his passport shortly after his loss, as the candidate faces a pair of federal money-laundering probes in Brazil and police there considered him a flight risk
President Donald Trump said on ⁠Saturday (October 31, 2026) evening that defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro can stay in the United States indefinitely.

"He can stay here as long as he wants," ‌Mr. Trump ⁠said of Mr. Bolsonaro, who left Brazil after losing the election to leftist incumbent ⁠Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, despite leading in most opinion polls. "In my opinion, the election was a disgrace," he added. Outside observers described the election as ​free and fair.
The Brazilian embassy in Washington did not immediately return a request for comment.

Mr. Bolsonaro's decision to go ‌to the U.S. followed a ruling by a Brazilian Supreme Court Justice to revoke his passport shortly after his loss, as the candidate faces a pair of federal money-laundering probes in Brazil and police there considered him a flight risk.
Flavio Bolsonaro says he left Brazil because he is the victim of 'persecution'
Flavio Bolsonaro claims he is Brazil’s true leader after fleeing to U.S.
He was admitted ‌to the United States under humanitarian parole, Reuters has previously reported, a status ​that typically only lasts for one year.

Mr. Rubio had said earlier on Saturday (October 31, 2026) that he spoke with Brazilian Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira at at the G20 Foreign Ministers’ meeting in Atlanta, and that they would see each other again in a few weeks.

A U.S. official and a person familiar with the matter have told Reuters that Mr. Trump has no current plans to support the political ambitions of Mr. Bolsonaro — who has described himself as Brazil's rightful leader — despite allowing the Brazilian politician into the ‌U.S. Mr. Trump, on Saturday (October 31, 2026), said he has no plans to meet with Mr. Bolsonaro.

Mr. Rubio said on Saturday (October 31, 2026) that ​the U.S. Government "was not involved directly in any of the moves" that led to Mr. Bolsonaro's departure from Brazil earlier this week. However, Reuters and several ⁠other media outlets have reported that Jason Miller, a White House official, helped arrange Mr. Bolsonaro's ⁠journey.

Mr. Bolsonaro's father, far-right former President Jair Bolsonaro, is imprisoned in Brazil for plotting a coup after losing his own re-election bid in 2022. Mr. Lula himself spent ‌17 months in jail in 2018 and 2019 on corruption charges that were later annulled.

articles.title: ‘Epstein Files’: U.S. Judge dismisses Trump lawsuit against Wall Street Journal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Donald Trump had sued for $10 billion after the newspaper’s story was published in July 2025 detailing the President’s alleged 2003 letter to Epstein, which apparently featured a drawing of a naked woman

A U.S. Judge on Saturday (October 31, 2026) dismissed President Donald Trump's defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal and media magnate Rupert Murdoch over a report that Mr. Trump sent a bawdy birthday letter to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Mr. Trump had sued for $10 billion after the newspaper's story was published in July 2025 detailing the President's alleged 2003 letter to Epstein, which apparently featured a drawing of a naked woman.
Mr. Murdoch is the founder of News Corp. which owns the Wall Street Journal.

The report piled scrutiny on Mr. Trump from both Democrats and his own Republican party, who rejected the President's attempts to downplay the saga as a hoax and called for a full release of legal files on Epstein.

In Saturday's (October 31, 2026) ruling, Judge Darrin Gayles dismissed Mr. Trump's lawsuit with prejudice, meaning Mr. Trump cannot file an amended version of the suit, as he did when Mr. Gayles turned down an initial version of it back in April.
The Judge wrote that in bringing his defamation claim, Mr. Trump had both times failed to establish that the defendants "acted with actual malice."
The House Oversight Committee last year published a copy of Mr. Trump's alleged birthday note to Epstein, which consists of a short dialogue between "Donald" and "Jeffrey."
"We have certain things in common," says Mr. Trump, to which Epstein responds: "Yes, we do, come to think of it."
"Enigmas never age, have you noticed that?" asks Mr. Trump.
"As a matter of fact, it was clear to me the last time I saw you," says Epstein.

"A pal is a wonderful thing. Happy Birthday — and may every day be another wonderful secret," the note ends, followed by Mr. Trump's signature, which takes the place of pubic hair on the nude outline.

Mr. Trump's supporters have been obsessed with the Epstein case for years and held as an article of faith that "deep state" elites were protecting a sex ring of Epstein associates, particularly in the Democratic Party and Hollywood.

articles.title: Ra’am and Joint List | The surge of the other
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Israel’s Arab parties made historic gains in elections but uncertainty remains whether the opposition bloc would join hands with them to form a government

On October 27, the day Israel went to the polls, the first election since the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack, the country recorded its highest voter turnout since 1999, at 77.7% But this was not the only story about the turnout.

Israel’s often overlooked Arab citizens, who make up some 20% of the population, made an overwhelming case for representation and change that day by turning out in massive numbers to vote. Exit polls recorded by Channel 12 estimated their turnout at nearly 80%, the highest in at least a decade.

For the far-right coalition led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu , the election was a “war for our home”, but for Arab parties, the political mobilisation meant meaningful representation in the Knesset , the Israeli parliament.

This mobilisation seems to have paid off. Arab parties have emerged as the third bloc after the elections. The Joint List and the United Arab List (Ra’am) have secured a combined 19 seats in the 120-member Parliament, their highest-ever tally.

Part of the credit goes to the Arab parties, which have actively mobilised their communities to vote. But much of it also goes to Mr. Netanyahu’s far-right government, whose policies and rhetoric, including the war on Gaza and escalating violence in the occupied West Bank, have heightened fears among Arab citizens.

While Arab citizens are affected like any other Israelis when it comes to national security, they’ve also borne the brunt of racism and violence. According to polls by the Israeli Democracy Institute, a party’s position related to crime in Arab society was one of the most important factors determining their vote.

Fear, as many experts have pointed out, has been their prime motivation, which Arab parties have been able to mobilise given the divisive campaigns launched by Mr. Netanyahu’s bloc. During the campaign, the Netanyahu camp put up billboards, saying it was ‘either the right or Palestine’. Even on the day of polling, the Prime Minister urged his supporters to go and vote, pointing to an Arab voter surge and calling it a matter of “life and death”.

While leaders of Arab parties have called Mr. Netanyahu’s attempts racist, they, too, have borne the brunt of discrimination. Like in the cases of previous elections, an attempt was made for disqualification of the Ra’am party and the Joint List (an alliance of Balad, Hadash and Ta’al) before the polls. The surge in voter turnout has helped them gain a significant number of seats, which would have made them kingmakers in a hung Parliament where no bloc has a clear majority. But neither side has expressed any willingness to form a government with Arab parties.

Mr. Netanyahu has accused the Arab parties of “stealing” the elections and has vowed to keep them out of power, while Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the opposition coalition, has been reluctant to join hands with them.

This reluctance is not new. The Ra’am party, led by Mansour Abbas, became the first Arab party in nearly 44 years to be part of a government in 2021 when they backed the Bennett-Yair Lapid government. Ra’am broke off from the Joint List. However, this experiment was short-lived as the coalition collapsed within a year. Ra’am returned to the opposition fold after Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition won the elections in 2022.
Arab parties had previously supported governments from outside, especially under Labour Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin.

For Arab parties, the question of coalition is not an easy take either. Any alliance with Jewish parties is challenging given how much they differ in their views on Palestine. Most Jewish parties, including Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud and Mr. Eisenkot’s Yashar, are opposed to the establishment of a Palestinian State and support the occupation of the West Bank.

articles.title: Taiwan says China harassing shipping with east coast patrol
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Taiwan's Coast Guard said China's "attempts to harass ships at sea through radio ‌communications are a clear expansion of power that violate international law, undermine regional peace and stability, and deviate from reality"

China's Coast Guard is harassing shipping with its latest patrol off Taiwan's east coast and trying ​to exert a fictional jurisdiction, the Taiwanese Coast Guard said, adding ‌it had sent its own ships to keep watch.

China, ​which views Taiwan as its own territory, ⁠has stepped up activity off the island's east coast since June with regular coast guard patrols. Officials in Taiwan, which rejects Beijing's sovereignty ‌claims, say they believe China is practising for a potential maritime blockade using overlapping military, paramilitary and ‌civilian assets.
Taipei regards the area off its east ‌coast ⁠as critical to wartime supply routes from allies ⁠in the event of a blockade or conflict. China recognises no claims of sovereignty by Taiwan.

Responding late on Saturday (October 31, 2026) to China's announcement of its latest ​east coast patrol, Taiwan's ‌Coast Guard said two Chinese ships were involved and it had sent its own forces to monitor.
Chinese state media showed video of one of its ships broadcasting a ‌radio message that it was carrying out law enforcement ​and offering help should any be needed.
It did not say who the message was ⁠broadcast at, but showed footage of an unidentified fishing trawler.

Taiwan's Coast Guard said China's "attempts to harass ships at sea through radio ‌communications are a clear expansion of power that violate international law, undermine regional peace and stability, and deviate from reality".
"Our country holds sovereign rights and jurisdiction over the exclusive economic zone east of Taiwan, and China has absolutely no jurisdiction over any of Taiwan's waters," it added.

China on ‌Saturday (October 31, 2026) also sent another Coast Guard ship close to the Taiwan-controlled Pratas ​Islands, which are strategically located at the top of the South China Sea, Taiwan's Coast Guard said ⁠separately.
Taiwan has so far this year "expelled" Chinese Coast Guard vessels from ⁠Pratas waters 13 times, it added.

The Pratas have no permanent civilian population and lie roughly between ‌southern Taiwan and Hong Kong. Security experts see them as vulnerable to Chinese attack due to their distance — ​more than 400 km (250 miles) — from Taiwan.

articles.title: Andhra civic polls: Jagan stages sit-in in Pulivendula, demands repoll; 37.13% turnout by 1 p.m. | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Fourteen vehicles were set on fire in Pulivendula, Kadapa district, Andhra Pradesh hours before polling began on Sunday

YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy staged a sit-in outside the Returning Officer’s office in Pulivendula on Sunday, demanding a repoll in the town.He alleged that YSRCP polling agents had been denied entry into several polling booths. He had gone to the office to raise the issue with the Returning Officer, but officials reportedly did not let him in. He then sat down outside in protest.

Jaya Kumar, 66, a senior citizen with ailments, made his way to the polling station at Chepala Thimmapuram, Ward 5, in Visakhapatnam on Sunday, leaning on a bamboo stick for support. At the compound, a wheelchair stood unoccupied beside the wall. The ramp, the usual access route for those unable to take the stairs, was packed with voters standing in the queue behind its handrails. Mr. Jaya Kumar was told by the staff on duty to walk around the building and use the stairs at the other end. The queue continued well past noon.

Andhra Pradesh’s overall turnout in the urban local body elections rose to 37.13% by 1 p.m. on Sunday, up from 22.08% at 11 a.m., according to the State Election Commission. About 35.97 lakh of the 96.89 lakh voters had cast their votes.

Kanigiri in Markapuram district recorded the highest turnout, 63.36%, though only two of its wards are voting. Jammalamadugu in Kadapa district, voting in all 32 wards, was close behind at 61.86%, followed by Nagari at 60.81%. Pulivendula, the scene of this morning’s clashes , 51.51% had voted.

Among the 13 corporations, Machilipatnam is well ahead at 47.85%. Vijayawada was at 36.40% and Guntur at 30.94%. Visakhapatnam, which had the second-lowest turnout at 11 a.m., is now the lowest of all the urban bodies at 27.55%. 1 pm - Poll Percentage.pdf

State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha and Secretary A. Mallikarjuna reviewed polling across the State through webcasting on Sunday. Some 13,500 CCTV cameras have been installed at polling stations, following the Supreme Court’s directions.

Nellore Collector and District Election Officer Himanshu Shukla rides a motorcycle to inspect polling stations in Nellore on Sunday. He visited several stations, including one at DSR High School in Moolapeta. Bike.jpeg Photo: Special Arrangement

Medical staff and voters attend to Pasupuleti Narasimha Rao, 70, who collapsed while arriving to vote at the Ramanagar Municipal School polling station in Ongole on Sunday. He was taken to a hospital. Photo: Kommuri Srinivas Collapsed.jpeg

The YSRCP “seems to have come ‘well-prepared’ in Kadapa” while the rest of the State is voting peacefully, Minister Nara Lokesh said in a post on X on Sunday. The election authorities would deal with “criminal elements”, he said, urging voters to turn out in large numbers.

Turnout in Kadapa district’s urban bodies stood at 25.46% by 11 a.m., above the State average of 22.08%, according to the State Election Commission’s figures. Jammalamadugu recorded 60.92% and Pulivendula 35.17%. Kadapa city, the district’s only corporation, was at 18.54%.

YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy accused the State Election Commission of failing to ensure a level playing field in the municipal elections and of siding with the ruling NDA government. Speaking to reporters in Pulivendula on Sunday (November 1, 2026), he said the SEC should give every candidate a fair chance from nominations to counting. “Only then it will be termed as an election,” he said.

He alleged that journalists had been beaten up and their cameras destroyed in Pulivendula. Polling agents were not allowed into polling stations, he claimed. The Centre should step in even though the TDP is its ally, he said. “If today an NDA partner is permitted to do so and the central government chooses to ignore it, then democracy will not prevail.”

articles.title: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy likens PM Modi to ‘Ravana’ and Congress to ‘Vanara Sena’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy said the Telangana contingent had arrived in Delhi to defeat Prime Minister Narendra Modi, whom he likened to Ravana, while describing the Congress cadre as a vanara sena.
Follow LIVE: INDIA bloc protest in Delhi on November 1, 2026

Addressing party leaders and workers at Telangana Bhavan, he said the Congress would wage a battle against alleged vote theft at the Ramlila Maidan rally. Claiming that 13.5 crore votes had already been deleted, he alleged that another seven crore votes could be removed in the coming days.
Mr. Reddy alleged that poor people were being targeted through the deletion of their votes and accused the BJP of conspiring to ensure that Mr. Modi returned to power.
Referring to the difficulties faced by party workers in travelling to Delhi, he said a large number of people from Telangana had reached the national capital despite trains being stopped.
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy waves to the congress cadre at the Telangana Bhavan in New Delhi on November 1, 2026. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement
Earlier, he arrived at the Telangana Bhavan, where he was accorded a warm welcome by Ministers, MPs, MLAs, MLCs, party leaders and workers who had gathered to participate in the Opposition rally.
Ministers, Legislators, MPs and party functionaries accompanied the Chief Minister, while party leaders and workers began moving towards Ramlila Maidan to attend the public meeting.

articles.title: Sonia, Rahul Gandhi, Mamata Banerjee among INDIA bloc leaders marching to Ramlila Maidan, demanding CEC's removal | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: INDA bloc's 'public impeachment' of CEC Gyanesh Kumar featured accounts from voters who alleged that their names had been deleted from electoral rolls

Rahul Gandhi, in a post on X, said he had told people coming for the march and mega rally to shop in the area. He alleged that, on reaching Connaught Place, he found “the BJP has forcibly shut down every single shop”, and said people should know who was causing losses to traders.

AICC general secretary K C Venugopal on Sunday said the party’s protest rally against CEC Gyanesh Kumar to be held during the day at Ramlila grounds in the national capital was a “stern warning” to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah.
Congress has alleged electoral irregularities and demanded the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
Mr. Venugopal told the media in Delhi that it will be a protest like never before and that it has affected the composure of the PM and Home Minister.

Senior INDIA bloc leaders, including Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav, TMC chief Mamata Banerjee, CPI(M) general secretary M.A. Baby, CPI general secretary D. Raja and CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya, reached Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s residence, from where they proceeded to Minto Road in an open bus to march to Ramlila Maidan.

Supporters have gathered at the venue, and party workers at locations across Delhi, ahead of the protest today (November 1, 2026) against alleged electoral irregularities and demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation.
Tribal communities from across the country performed a cultural dance in Connaught Place ahead of the INDIA bloc’s rally at Ramlila Ground.

Congress leader and Punjab Congress in-charge Sachin Pilot said the government wants to stop people through pressure and prevent them from voicing their opinions, but neither Rahul Gandhi nor “our people” would back down. He said “hundreds of thousands” would arrive from across the country today (November 1, 2026) and that traders would see “a lot of business”.

Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, speaking in Shimla, alleged that Mr. Gandhi was upset because the names of “infiltrators” had been removed through the SIR. He said the BJP stood with the Election Commission. He asked whether the elections in Himachal Pradesh, Kerala and Mr. Gandhi’s own Raebareli seat should be annulled by the same logic, and accused the Congress of “double standards” for claiming votes are “stolen” only where the BJP is in power. He also made an insulting personal remark against Mr. Gandhi.

Mr. Nadda called the Ramlila Maidan rally “a foolish, orchestrated drama”. He alleged that Mr. Gandhi’s politics works in four stages: spreading lies and rumours, inciting street anarchy, damaging the economy, and destabilising an elected government “at the behest of foreign powers”. He said the rally had four aims, among them to “rub salt into the wounds” of Sikhs and to rob Delhi traders of festive-season earnings.
Union Minister J.P. Nadda told Rahul Gandhi that India was “not some ‘banana republic’” where one could “incite arson, trigger riots, or push an agenda for ‘regime change’”.

He called November 1 the “darkest stain” in India’s democratic history, alleging that “goons nurtured by the Congress party” massacred Sikhs on this day in 1984, and said the Gandhi family had never offered a sincere apology. articles.title: Mysuru City Corporation collects ₹210 crore in property tax so far this year: Yathindra Siddaramaiah
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mysuru City Corporation had set a target of collecting ₹286.72 crore in property tax during 2026-27
Minister in charge of Mysuru district Yathindra Siddaramaiah said the Mysuru City Corporation (MCC) has collected ₹210 crore in property tax so far during the current financial year.

He was delivering his Rajyothsava Day address in Mysuru on Sunday (November 1, 2026). It may be mentioned here that the MCC had set a target of collecting ₹286.72 crore in property tax during 2026-27.

During his address, Mr. Yathindra said a special ‘Prajaseva’ e-Khata campaign by charging a nominal fee of just ₹175 had been organised by MCC recently. During the campaign, over 590 property owners had been distributed e-khata documents within 72 hours of submitting their applications.
So far, around 78,000 ‘A’ and ‘B’ Khatas have been issued in MCC, he added.

GRAMANUBHAVA: Mr. Yathindra also launched the ‘Gramanubhava’ or Village Experience programme, an initiative by the State Government’s Department of School Education and Literacy aimed at creating awareness among urban students about rural life, agricultural culture, and their connection to the soil.
AWARDS: Meanwhile, a total of 92 persons were given away district level Rajyothsava awards on the occasion.
Also, SSLC and PUC students who studied in the Kannada medium at Government schools and secured the high marks were felicitated.

Narasimharaja Assembly constituency MLA Tanveer Sait, MLCs C.N. Manjegowda and Raghu, Deputy Commissioner G. Lakshmikanth Reddy, Zilla Panchayat CEO S. Yukesh Kumar, Mysuru City Police Commissioner Seema Latkar, Mysuru City Corporation Commissioner M.K. Savitha, Additional Deputy Commissioner R. Aishwarya along with other officials, pro-Kannada activists, and dignitaries were present at the event.

articles.title: Foolish drama, will be final nail in coffin of Congress' political future: Nadda
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Union Minister Nadda alleged that the protest was part of a well-thought-out conspiracy to surrender democracy to anarchy and disorder

Union Minister J.P. Nadda on Sunday (November 1, 2026) slammed the Opposition INDIA bloc's rally as a "foolish and designed drama" and said it will prove to be the final "nail in the coffin" of Congress' "political downfall".
Mr. Nadda alleged that the protest was part of a well-thought-out conspiracy to surrender democracy to anarchy and disorder.
INDIA block protest rally at Ramlila Maidan LIVE updates

In an apparent reference to the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, Mr. Nadda claimed that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's objective behind organising it on Sunday was to rub salt into the wounds of "Sikh brothers".

"Removing the democratically elected government by conspiring to spread riots and anarchy in Delhi, adversely impacting the earnings of shopkeepers and traders in Delhi during the festive season and defaming the country are other objectives of the rally," the senior BJP leader told reporters.

"The day of November 1 is the ugliest and darkest blot on India's democratic history. On this very day, goons patronised by Congress massacred our innocent Sikh brothers. Thousands and lakhs of Sikh families became homeless overnight."
Mr. Nadda said India is a strong democracy and will not be run by riot-based politics, but by the Constitution and the mandate of the people.
“Whatever is happening today at Ramlila Maidan is not respect for democracy, but a well-thought-out conspiracy to surrender democracy to anarchy and disorder.
"This is a foolish and designed drama of people who have been defeated and repeatedly rejected by the public. The public understands this very well,” he charged.

The Opposition alliance is holding the 'Chalo Dilli' protest in the national capital as part of its campaign against alleged electoral irregularities and demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

"Rahul Gandhi, listen carefully. You cannot hide the dark history of November 1. You cannot escape answering for the tears of Delhi's traders," Mr. Nadda said, adding, "Your rally will prove to be the final nail in the coffin of Congress' political downfall."

articles.title: Six Indian tourists stranded in Nepal, rescue efforts underway
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Indian tourists had ventured into the area despite warnings from security personnel and the Nepali guide accompanying them, says an official

Security personnel are making efforts to rescue six Indian tourists, including two women, stranded due to heavy snowfall in the Shey-Phoksundo National Park area of Nepal since Saturday afternoon (October 31, 2026), officials said on Sunday (November 1, 2026).
The tourists had gone to the Dho area in Shey Phoksundo Rural Municipality’s Ward No. 8, which was covered in heavy snow, according to Dolpa Chief District Officer Junu Dhakal.
Shey Phoksundo Lake, located in the rural municipality, is Nepal’s deepest lake. It is situated at an altitude of 3,600 metres and has an estimated depth of 145 metres.
“We have located the area where they are stranded, and an Army helicopter is arriving to rescue them. We hope to rescue them soon,” Ms. Dhakal told PTI .
The Indian tourists had ventured into the area despite warnings from security personnel and the Nepali guide accompanying them, she said.
Ms. Dhakal said the tourists left the guide and proceeded towards the lake area despite heavy snowfall. Communication with them was disrupted on Saturday night (October 31, 2026).

The guide contacted the District Administration Office in Dolpa on Saturday evening (October 31, 2026), saying the tourists might have been stranded due to heavy snowfall, she said. However, communication was completely disrupted on Sunday morning (November 1, 2026).
“We cannot say they are missing, as we have located the area,” Ms. Dhakal clarified.

The tourists have been identified as Moumita Halder, Piyali Koley, Jajla Trivedi Kumar, Aditya Singha, Diplina Bishwas and Rajesh De, according to a press release issued by the District Administration Office, Dolpa.
Security personnel are being mobilised, and a rescue helicopter is expected to arrive soon, the press release said.

articles.title: Terrorism is 'red line': Pakistan tells Afghanistan as it warns of action against cross-border threats
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting of Pakistan, on Saturday, accused the Afghan Taliban leadership of refusing to address militancy emanating from Afghan soil and instead shifting blame on Islamabad for the deterioration in bilateral ties

Pakistan has warned Afghanistan that it reserves the right to take all necessary measures to eliminate cross-border terror threats , asserting that terrorism remains a "red line" and its national security cannot be held hostage to the Taliban regime's "inaction".

In a strongly worded statement issued Saturday (October 31, 2026) night, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting accused the Afghan Taliban leadership of refusing to address militancy emanating from Afghan soil and instead shifting blame on Islamabad for the deterioration in bilateral ties.
The latest remarks by the Afghan Taliban spokesperson exposed the regime's “deeply misguided approach and unwillingness to confront the root cause of deteriorating relations with Pakistan”, it said.
"Pakistan’s position is unequivocal: Terrorism is a red line and the security of its citizens is non-negotiable,” the Ministry said.
The statement came in response to remarks made by Afghan Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid, who accused Pakistan of being unwilling to resolve tensions with Afghanistan through dialogue.

In an interview to Hurriyat Radio on Saturday (October 31, 2026), the spokesperson said Islamabad lacked the necessary readiness for a peaceful resolution of differences and its “wrong policies” were preventing a resolution of the conflict.
Afghanistan was not responsible for the counter-terrorism issues cited by Pakistan, he said.

Pakistan said the Afghan Taliban regime must understand that Islamabad will "not tolerate terrorist sanctuaries across its borders that impact its security nor allow its people to remain targets of terrorism emanating from Afghanistan”.

The Taliban leadership continues to blame Islamabad’s policies while conveniently ignoring the single most important issue poisoning bilateral relations, which is its persistent failure to address terrorism emanating from Afghan soil, the statement said.

"The Taliban regime's persistent refusal to address terrorism remains the principal obstacle to normal relations. Shifting blame, making hollow assurances and questioning Pakistan’s policies will neither resolve the crisis nor absolve Kabul of its responsibilities,” it said.
Afghan forces struck militant hideouts in Pakistan: Taliban
Pakistan air strikes kill four civilians in Afghanistan: Kabul

articles.title: Israeli protesters demand opposition ally with Arab parties to oust Netanyahu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Arab-majority parties made major gains in elections, fuelled by anger over rhetoric targeting the community from Mr. Netanyahu’s hard-right government, but opposition chief Gadi Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition with them

Hundreds of Israelis took to the streets on Saturday (October 31, 2026) to urge the opposition to ally with Arab parties to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu , who has gone on the offensive against the minority group's leaders.

Arab-majority parties made major gains in Tuesday’s election, fuelled by anger over rhetoric targeting the community from Mr. Netanyahu’s hard-right government, but opposition chief Gadi Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition with them.
Joining a rally in Tel Aviv, Ayelet Raz said that the Arab community, which accounts for around 20% of Israel's population, had a right to political participation.
"It's the last chance for real change," the 60-year-old psychologist said, warning that Mr. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister, was a "great manipulator".
"We need to give peace a chance," she said. "Otherwise we'll have this bloodshed forever."
Tuesday’s election was inconclusive, with neither bloc reaching a majority in Israel's 120-seat parliament.
Jewish-majority parties opposed to Mr. Netanyahu, known by his nickname Bibi, won 48 seats, while two Arab-majority parties, Raam and the Joint List, secured a combined 19 seats.
An alliance between the two camps would potentially give the anti-Netanyahu bloc a comfortable majority of 67 seats, but the idea is opposed by some parties in the opposition bloc.
"Arabs and Jews will only win together" and "There is a majority for change" read some of the signs held by around 500 protesters in Tel Aviv.
"67 — United we stand, divided we get Bibi" and "Why not, really — unless we are racist?" read some of the placards at the 100-strong rally in Jerusalem.

Arab parties have only once formally sat in an Israeli government, when Raam leader Mansour Abbas joined a short-lived coalition that lasted from 2021 to 2022. He has voiced a willingness to do so again.
The Joint List's Yousef Jabareen, meanwhile, has told AFP he is willing to support Mr. Eisenkot in parliament without joining his government, citing, among other concerns, the war in Gaza.

articles.title: Health Wrap Episode 57 discusses mapping the human brain, potential of brain atlases and more
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The episode discusses a new technology developed at IIT Madras to create detailed three-dimensional maps of the human brain, the recently released C-STROKE atlas and plans to map more than 100 brains
The 57th episode of Health Wrap by The Hindu explores how researchers are using advanced imaging and reconstruction techniques to create detailed, three-dimensional maps of the human brain.

Zubeda Hamid, senior assistant editor, The Hindu, speaks to Mohanasankar Sivaprakasam, Head of the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at IIT Madras, about the technology, how the maps are created and what they could reveal about the human brain.

The episode looks at C-STROKE, a recently released three-dimensional atlas of a stroke-affected brain. Unlike conventional MRI scans, which provide images of the brain at a particular resolution, the new approach allows researchers to examine brain structures in greater detail and build comprehensive 3D maps.

The discussion explains how researchers prepare brain tissue, use imaging techniques and reconstruct the data to create these maps. It also looks at the different scientific and technological disciplines involved in the process and how detailed mapping could help researchers study the brain’s structure and changes associated with neurological conditions.

Another focus is the Centre’s plan to map more than 100 human brains across different stages of life. The project aims to build a larger collection of brain maps that could help researchers understand variations in brain structure, study neurological conditions and expand the available resources for brain research.

The episode also examines the potential applications of these atlases in clinical research and healthcare, including how they could contribute to a better understanding of stroke and other brain conditions. It discusses the possibilities as well as the work needed before such maps can be translated into clinical applications.
The episode can also be viewed on The Hindu health page along with the full playlist of The Health Wrap

articles.title: How infant deaths in Keralam’s Attappady expose a deep-rooted health, social crisis
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: 12 infants, including 10 tribals, have died in Attappady this year, sparking a political row as the State government orders an expert probe. Tribal activists say the crisis demands action beyond healthcare, addressing malnutrition, anaemia and deep-rooted social issues

The deaths of 12 infants, 10 of them from tribal communities, in Attappady in Keralam in recent months have once again cast a spotlight on a child health crisis that has defied solutions for over a decade. While the State government has set an expert assessment in motion, tribal organisations maintain that the roots of the crisis run deeper than healthcare, demanding sustained action on nutrition, maternal health, landlessness and the wider socio-economic conditions of the community.

Figures cited by tribal activists show that 124 infants have died in the region since 2011. Since 2012, Attappady has also recorded around 300 abortions, 90 intrauterine deaths and two dozen stillbirths. The region came under particular scrutiny in 2013, when 47 tribal infants died. Tribal observers estimate that around 10 children have died annually over the years.

articles.title: Captain Chowta opposes proposal to revise timings of Gomateshwara Express
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Railway Ministry’s plan to postpone Mangaluru Junction-Yeshwantpur tri-weekly and weekly express departure timing from 7 am to 11.40 am severely affects passengers

Dakshina Kannada Member of Parliament Captain Brijesh Chowta has taken strong exceptions to Railway Ministry’s proposal to revise the departure timing of Mangaluru Junction – Yeshwantpur tri-weekly and weekly expresses from Mangaluru.

In a letter to Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Saturday, October 31, Capt. Chowta said he understood the Ministry was proposing to shift the departure timing from the present 7:00 a.m. to 11:40 a.m. for Train No. 16576, Mangaluru Junction-Yeshwantpur tri-weekly Gomateshwara Express, and Train No. 16540, Mangaluru Junction-Yeshwantpur weekly Express, as a consequence of which their arrival time at Yeshwantpur would be postponed from 4:30 p.m. to 10:15 p.m. Such a substantial change would affect the convenience and accessibility of this important daytime connection.

He said the existing daytime train service between Bengaluru and Mangaluru is an important and widely utilised rail connection for people travelling between the two regions. Its current schedule has been particularly convenient for daily and frequent passengers, including students, working professionals, business travellers, patients and families.

The MP said the present schedule allows passengers to undertake their journey during the day and reach Bengaluru at a reasonable hour. Shifting the departure to late morning and arrival to late evening would cause considerable inconvenience, particularly to passengers who depend on this service for work, education, medical appointments and onward travel.

“Given the importance of the Bengaluru-Mangaluru rail corridor and the considerable passenger dependence on this service, I request the Ministry of Railways and South Western Railway to kindly reconsider the proposed changes and retain the existing timings of the Yesvantpur-Mangaluru Express and its return service,” he said.

“Any changes to the schedules of established passenger services should be undertaken after due consideration of passenger requirements and consultations with relevant stakeholders,” the MP told the Ministry.

fullParagraphs: Supporters have gathered at the venue, and party workers at locations across Delhi, against alleged electoral irregularities and demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation.
nion Home Minister Amit Shah said Delhi traders had repeatedly urged the Congress to postpone its November 1 rally until after Diwali, citing concerns over festival-season business.

Union Minister JP Nadda accused Rahul Gandhi of attempting to incite unrest and destabilise the elected government through the rally at Ramlila Maidan. He also invoked the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, accusing the Congress of having a dark record on the issue.

AISA president Neha Bora said that removing people’s names from electoral rolls denied them equal status and made them “second-class citizens”. She alleged that Muslims, women, Dalits, Adivasis and poor labourers were repeatedly asked to prove their citizenship.

Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi claimed that 15% of India’s voters were removed from electoral rolls after the 2024 elections, alleging that this made the election “illegal” and “stolen”. He said the Election Commission had made the claim. ANI/Congress

Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde criticised the INDIA bloc’s rally at Ramlila Maidan, alleging that its leaders were spreading a “fake narrative” and defaming Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the INDIA bloc would not be intimidated by the police, CBI, Enforcement Directorate or other government agencies.

Addressing the ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ rally at Ramlila Maidan, he accused the BJP of trying to divide people and “snatch” their votes. He called for support to remove the Modi government, saying it was necessary to save democracy.

articles.title: Karnataka thinking of officially recognising Kannada flag: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The State Government will also issue order to enable private institutions to fly Kannada flag and it is thinking of making flying of the Kannada flag mandatory in institutions supported by government

The Karnataka Government is thinking of officially recognising the Kannada flag, and that the issue would be discussed in the ensuing Winter legislature session at Belagavi scheduled to commence from November 30, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said on Sunday (November 1, 2026).

The State Government will also issue order to enable private institutions to fly Kannada flag and it is thinking of making flying of the Kannada flag mandatory in institutions supported by the government.

“I have hoisted the Kannada flag along with the national flag. We are eager to officially recognise the Kannada flag. This will help take the footprint of Karnataka to greater heights in India’s federal structure,” he said. He spoke to reporters near his residence and Vidhan Soudha, as well as in his address at the 71st Rajyothsava celebrations at Kanteerava Stadium.

“In the past, the Cabinet had cleared the proposal to officially recognise the Kannada flag and the proposal had been submitted to the Centre, which is yet to accord approval. Recently, the issue has been discussed with legal experts and another round of discussion will be held. Legal options will be explored to officially recognise the Kannada flag without dishonouring the national flag or in violation of rules pertaining to the national flag,” the Chief Minister said.

In 2018, the State Government, then headed by Mr. Siddaramaiah, had approved a horizontal tricolour flag with yellow, white and red, with the insignia of Gandaberunda (a mythical bird and the State’s emblem) in the Centre after an expert committee set up by the Kannada and Culture Department recommended the design. The proposal was sent to the Centre since it requires an amendment to the Flag Code that governs national flag-related issues, and the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) turned it down. Mr. Shivakumar, however, said, “There will be no addition. This [pointing at Kannada and yellow] will be our flag. This is what has been accepted by people and us.”

Further, Mr. Shivakumar said that the issue of according official status to the State flag would be discussed again in the Cabinet. “Our Government is committed to bringing legislation to ensure hoisting the state flag along with the national flag. The issue is open for discussion in public and among the legislators, and it will be given a new life in the winter session. Our Government is committed for a resolution seeking official status for the State flag and ensuring legal protection. This is not our government, this is your government. The Kannada flag is the beacon of emotions of Kannadigas, and it will be respected. We are taking steps to officially recognise the Kannada flag that symbolises Kannada knowledge, culture, heritage, a culture of equality for all religions and peace.”

Mr. Shivakumar also announced that the State Government has made preparations to organise various programmes to create awareness about the eminence of Kannada for the next one year. “The Kannada flag will be hoisted in all Government offices, and the government is thinking of making flying Kannada flags compulsory in institutions supported by the State Government. The government will issue an order this month to enable private institutions to fly the Kannada flag.”

Asking the Kannada activists not to indulge in ‘moral policing’ in IT and other companies, the Chief Minister told presspersons, “Marathi-speaking people should also have to accept the Rajyothsava since they are living here. Those who are here [non-Kannada-speaking population] should live here restpectfully. When we are trying to withdraw all cases against Kannada activists, they should not indulge in moral policing. The Government is there to protect the interest of the State.”

articles.title: Lady Goshen stands first among district government hospitals for zero maternal mortality after abortion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A survey conducted by the Health and Family Welfare Department in collaboration with Ipas Development Foundation among district hospitals in the State has recognised the Lady Goschen to this distinction, said a release

The District Government Lady Goschen Hospital has secured the first place in the State for maintaining 100% maternal health and bringing maternal mortality to zero in legal abortion and post-abortion care performed during 2025-26.

A survey conducted by the Health and Family Welfare Department in collaboration with Ipas Development Foundation among district hospitals in the State has recognised the Lady Goschen to this distinction, said a release. The hospital could reduce maternal and infant mortality rates to a minimum by adopting many innovative programs and methods.

The release said Lady Goschen has handled 304 legal abortions during the year under the survey, and each case has followed all the rules under the quality comprehensive abortion care program, recording a zero mortality rate.
It conducted 191 abortions before nine weeks of pregnancy, 31 between 10-12 weeks, 52 between 12-20 weeks, 20 between 20-24 weeks and five abortions post-24 weeks.

Hospital Medical Superintendent M. R. Durgaprasad congratulated the experts of the Obstetrics and Gynecology Department, Anesthesia Department, Radiodiagnosis Department, and Neonatal Department of KMC Hospital for their cooperation in achieving the feat.

He also said the service of the nursing staff, paramedical staff, and technical staff of the hospital was unique. Dr. Durgaprasad said the newly implemented WhatsApp High Risk Pregnancy Tracking System, Maternity Intensive Care Unit, Maternity Critical Care Unit, and High Risk Pregnancy Delivery Unit have played a major role in reducing the maternal mortality rate to zero.

The Medical Superintendent said the state-of-the-art life-saving equipment, which has been procured through corporate social responsibility grants from various organisations, has been helpful in providing quality service facilities. He appreciated the cooperation of the Health Minister, people’s representatives, senior officers of the district administration, departmental officers and social organisations in hospital’s functioning.

articles.title: Petrol export duty cut to nil, diesel levy raised by ₹3 a litre
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The government’s fortnightly review raised the export levy on diesel to ₹11.5 per litre from ₹8.5 and on aviation turbine fuel to ₹11 per litre from ₹10.5, while India’s diesel exports touched 700 kilo barrels per day in October, the highest since September 2025, according to Kpler

The government on Saturday (October 31, 2026) slashed the export duty on petrol to nil while hiking the levy on export of diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) by ₹3 per litre and 50 paise per litre respectively for the next 15-day period.
There was no change in the existing excise duty rates for petrol and diesel for domestic consumption.
Diesel exports would now draw a levy of ₹11.5 for every litre against ₹8.5 per litre it drew in the previous fortnight.
ATF would be subject to an export levy of ₹11 for every litre against ₹10.5 for every litre as mandated for the previous fortnight.
The revised levy on diesel assumes significance as India spiked its exports of the liquid vehicular fuel amid a global supply crunch, particularly in Europe.
According to data from real-time analytics provider Kpler, India’s diesel exports stood at 700 kilo barrels per day in October, the highest since September 2025.

Sumit Ritolia, Manager for Modelling and Refining at Kpler, in a social media post on Friday (October 30, 2026) further observed, “India’s diesel exports are expected to ease to 500-550 kbd in Nov–Dec as seasonal domestic demand peaks before recovering to 550–600 kbd in Q1 2027. Higher maintenance in Q2-27 will constrain export, with new capacity contributing meaningfully only later in 2027.”

The government has been conducting a fortnightly review of export levies since March 27, in the backdrop of the conflict in West Asia. These are done based on the average international benchmark prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF observed since the previous review.
This is to ensure the domestic availability of retail fuels by disincentivising exports.

articles.title: Kannada is a confluence of history, culture and diverse literary traditions: Priyank Kharge
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Emphasising the importance of preserving the State’s cultural heritage, Mr. Kharge said the present generation must protect its literature, history and traditions and pass them on to future generations

Kannada is not merely a language but a confluence of emotions, history, ideas, and traditions, said Home Minister and Kalaburagi in-charge Priyank Kharge, highlighting Karnataka’s rich literary and cultural heritage on the occasion of the 71st Karnataka Rajyotsava celebrations on Sunday (November 1, 2026).

After unfurling the national flag at the Nagareshwara High School premises in the Gunj area of Kalaburagi, Mr. Kharge addressed the gathering and said Kannada has a history spanning nearly 2,000 years and an exceptionally rich and diverse literary tradition.

He recalled that more than 40 foreign ambassadors had recently been invited by the State government to participate in the Dasara celebrations. During his interaction with them, the ambassadors had expressed admiration for Karnataka’s art, literature, food and culture. They were particularly surprised to learn about the antiquity of the Kannada language and its literary heritage, he said.

Kannada literature encompasses a rich diversity of traditions, ranging from folk and Dasa Sahitya to Jain and the Bandaya literary movements. Such a wide-ranging literary spectrum is rarely found in any other language, he observed.

Explaining Karnataka’s cultural diversity, Mr. Kharge said the State represented different identities and aspirations for different regions and communities. While Malnad was known for its lush greenery, Kalyana Karnataka was celebrated as the land of tur dal and Sufi saints, and the Mandya region as the land of silk and milk. The coastal region represented a distinctive cultural identity.

He described Karnataka as a land of art and culture for writers, a land that propagated the message of equality for followers of Basavanna, a centre of knowledge for the world, a land of opportunities for the youth, and a hub of human resources for foreigners.
He added that Karnataka’s diversity and human resources had made a significant contribution to the country’s economic progress.

Emphasising the importance of preserving the State’s cultural heritage, Mr. Kharge said the present generation must protect its literature, history and traditions and pass them on to future generations.

Celebrating Rajyotsava once a year should not be the sole expression of pride in Karnataka’s heritage. There should be sustained efforts to familiarise younger generations with the State’s cultural and literary legacy, he said.
Creating an environment conducive to preserving this heritage was the responsibility of elected representatives, while citizens also had an important role to play, he added.

The Minister joined the procession and enthusiastically played the drums. Students from various educational institutions, officials from different departments and people from various walks of life participated in the celebrations.

articles.title: Swimmer’s ear doesn’t just affect swimmers – two ear doctors explain what you need to know about this painful condition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Swimmer’s ear is an infection in the external ear canal, the tube leading from the ear opening to the eardrum. Typically, swimmer’s ear occurs only in one ear, and sometimes the eardrum itself is affected
Many forms of ear infections strike children and adults alike, but among the most common is acute otitis externa , also known as swimmer’s ear.
About 10% of Americans will experience swimmer’s ear during their lifetimes . Adults are affected more commonly , and children only rarely, generally ages 5 to 12.

But you don’t have to be swimming to get swimmer’s ear. Go out jogging or walking, or do yardwork on a hot day, and moisture from perspiration can drip in your ear. However, the occurrence increases fivefold in swimmers – thus the reason the condition came to be called “swimmer’s ear.” It also occurs more frequently in tropical climates because of humidity and higher temperatures.

As doctors who specialise in ear problems, we are actively involved in research and clinical treatment for children and adults struggling with ear, nose and throat problems. Practicing in the state of Florida, we’ve certainly seen our share of patients with swimmer’s ear.

Swimmer’s ear is an infection in the external ear canal, the tube leading from the ear opening to the eardrum. Typically, swimmer’s ear occurs only in one ear, and sometimes the eardrum itself is affected. Moisture trapped in the canal leads to a break in the skin barrier and creates an opening for certain bacteria types to enter or existing ones to overgrow.

One of these culprits is the bacterium Pseudomonas aeruginosa, which is present in soil and water throughout the world. These bacteria favor moist areas, such as sinks, toilets, inadequately chlorinated swimming pools and hot tubs, as well as outdated or inactivated antiseptic solutions.

If you have the infection, you’ll know it. Symptoms generally appear a few days after infection. The main symptom of swimmer’s ear is severe pain and discomfort. It’s particularly noticeable when the outer ear is tugged, or by touching the tragus – that’s the small bump at the front of your ear. Other symptoms include itchiness inside the ear, redness, swelling and drainage. A feeling of fullness, or the perception of a plugged ear, may also occur, along with disturbed balance and temporary hearing loss.

Numerous factors can predispose someone to swimmer’s ear . They include a narrow ear canal, and skin diseases such as eczema or psoriasis. In addition, individuals wearing ear plugs, ear buds or hearing aids may be at an increased risk. Diabetics may also be more prone to the infection .
Swimmer’s ear can also come from something getting stuck inside the ear, excessive ear cleaning or contact with chemicals in hair dye or hairspray.

Swimmer’s ear is diagnosed after a health care provider has gathered a thorough history and examined the inside of the ear. The ear canal will typically look red, swollen and moist. There is also a possibility of fluid drainage or the appearance of scaly, shedding skin. Depending on the degree of swelling, the eardrum may be hard to see. A sample of fluid may be removed from the ear and sent to a lab to look for bacteria or fungus.
Eardrops are commonly used to treat swimmer’s ear . These drops often contain antibiotics to kill the infection and steroids to stop the swelling.

One such eardrop is Ciprodex . It contains ciprofloxacin, an antibiotic, and dexamethasone, a powerful steroid. Patients will need to place about four to five drops in the infected ear canal twice a day for seven to 10 days.

articles.title: There’s new guidance on menopause symptoms like hot flashes. What women need to know
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: For the first time in a dozen years, a leading OB-GYN group has updated its guidance on managing hot flashes, night sweats, sleep changes and other disruptive symptoms that often come along with menopause
For the first time in a dozen years, a leading OB-GYN group has updated its guidance on managing hot flashes, night sweats, sleep changes and other disruptive symptoms that often come with menopause.

Doctors stressed the importance of hormone therapies, which many women are considering again after the removal of federal safety warnings. On Friday, federal officials said the Food and Drug Administration has been taking steps to ensure there's an adequate supply.
Doctors also described various nonhormonal options in the new advice released this month by the American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists, or ACOG.
“We would love our patients to go to their OB-GYNs regarding questions about menopause and really advocate for getting the treatment that they need,” said Camille Clare, the group’s president.

Menopause occurs when a woman has gone 12 consecutive months without a menstrual period. In the U.S., it usually happens around age 50. The time leading up to it is called perimenopause, during which the body’s production of the hormones estrogen and progesterone declines sharply.

Problems commonly arise. More than half of women in menopause report having “vasomotor” issues such as hot flashes and night sweats, said ACOG. As many as two-thirds report menopause-related sleep disruption. And more than a third of perimenopausal and postmenopausal women worldwide report depressive symptoms.
In the past, doctors said, many women quietly suffered.

There's growing consensus that "these symptoms should be treated,” said JoAnn Manson, a professor of medicine at Harvard Medical School. “This should help to empower women to discuss their symptoms with their healthcare provider.”
Manson said ACOG’s new guidelines are similar to those put out by other medical organizations.

"Moderate to severe or bothersome menopausal symptoms should be treated with hormone therapy as the first line of treatment,” she said. While it's not appropriate for all women, she added, it’s a good option for many.

In 2002, a landmark study in women taking a pill-based combination of estrogen and progestin was stopped early because of links to breast cancer, blood clots and other serious issues. Concerns lingered even though later studies showed the benefits of today’s hormone therapies outweigh the risks for many women. For more than 22 years, all hormone-based menopause treatments carried a government warning, which Manson said discouraged patients and doctors from using them.

But last year, the FDA announced it would remove the boxed warning from more than 20 pills, patches and creams containing the hormones estrogen and progestin. On Friday, the FDA approved updated labeling for three additional estrogen-based patches.
